records.abstract: A referee-free, axiom-clean Lean development of coding-theory certificates: syndrome decoding soundness and lossiness bounds for GF(2) parity-check schemes (with a Reed–Solomon evaluation-dual variant), and a fully machine-checked correctness proof of the Karp reduction chain 3SAT ≤ 3DM ≤ X3C ≤ bounded-weight syndrome decoding. Only the logical iff of each reduction is formalized; polynomial-time bounds, NP classes, and Cook–Levin are unformalized external inputs, so NP-hardness of decoding is conditional on those standard facts.

informal.Sundog.SATReductionMain.sat_iff_decodes: The end-to-end reduction correctness: a formula is satisfiable iff its image under the composed 3SAT-to-decoding reduction is a yes-instance of bounded-weight syndrome decoding.
informal.Sundog.MatchingNPHard.threeDM_iff_X3C: The 3-dimensional matching instance has a perfect matching iff the reduced exact-cover-by-3-sets instance has an exact cover, both directions machine-checked.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.accept_sound: Soundness of the cheap syndrome-decoding verifier when it accepts: an exhibited light same-syndrome witness certifies the body is safe within the decoding radius.
informal.Sundog.Certificate.reject_sound: Soundness of the verifier when it rejects: a sound column-weight lower bound on the minimum same-syndrome weight rules out every light witness, so the body is genuinely unsafe.

records.title: Synthetic Euclidean geometry: Euclid's Elements Book I
records.abstract: Formalizes Book I of Euclid's Elements via an axiomatic synthetic-geometry system (incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area), culminating in the Pythagorean theorem and its converse.

informal.SyntheticEuclid4.IncidenceGeometry: The axiomatic class of synthetic Euclidean geometry, bundling points, lines, circles, and the incidence, betweenness, congruence, and area primitives with Euclid's axioms.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.square_of_len: Constructs a square on a given segment off a given line.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_construct: Constructs the three squares and parallelograms on the sides of a triangle used in the proof of the Pythagorean theorem.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras: Euclid I.47, the Pythagorean theorem, that the square on the hypotenuse of a right triangle equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
informal.SyntheticEuclid4.pythagoras_converse: Euclid I.48, the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, that a triangle whose square areas satisfy the Pythagorean relation has a right angle.

records.title: The Three-Gap (Steinhaus) Theorem
records.abstract: Formalizes the three-gap (Steinhaus, three-distance) theorem: for every real `a` and every `N`, the `N`-point orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` partitions `[0,1)` into gaps taking at most three distinct lengths, and when exactly three occur the largest is the sum of the other two. The proof works in `[0,1)` via `Int.fract` (not `AddCircle`) through the two first-return times `η⁺` and `η⁻`, and is uniform in the rotation number, covering rational and irrational `a` with no case split.

informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_card_le_thre: For every real `a` and natural `N`, the gaps of the orbit `{i·a mod 1 : i < N}` take at most three distinct lengths.
informal.SteinhausThreeGap.three_gap_lengths_eq: When the gaps take exactly three distinct lengths, those lengths are precisely the two first returns `η⁺`, `η⁻`, and their sum `η⁺ + η⁻`; in particular the largest gap is the sum of the other two.

records.title: Turán's theorem (the "Book" weighting proof)
records.abstract: Formalizes the weighting/optimization proof of Turán's theorem from Proofs from THE BOOK, bounding the number of edges of a p-clique-free simple graph by (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n².

informal.Turan3.turans: Turán's theorem — a p-clique-free simple graph on n vertices has at most (1/2)(1 - 1/(p-1)) n² edges.
informal.Turan3.finale_bound: For any weight distribution on a p-clique-free graph, the total edge weight is at most ((p-1)(p-2)/2)·(1/(p-1))², the bound used to derive the edge count.
informal.Turan3.Better_forms_clique: Starting from any weight function, the minimal-support weight-non-decreasing improvement has support that forms a clique.
informal.Turan3.Enhance_total_weight_stricinc: Equalizing weights between a maximum- and minimum-weight vertex in the clique support strictly increases the total edge weight.

records.title: Ulm's theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups
records.abstract: Formalizes Ulm's classification theorem for countable reduced abelian p-groups in arbitrary Lean universes. The development constructs the transfinite Ulm filtration and invariants, proves their invariance under additive equivalence, establishes Kaplansky's one-generator extension lemma, and completes the countable back-and-forth classification. A finite-group regression distinguishes Z/4 x Z/4 from Z/2 x Z/8 at the zeroth Ulm invariant.

informal.UlmsTheorem.ulm_theorem: For any prime p and any two countable reduced abelian p-groups in the same arbitrary Lean universe, the groups are additively isomorphic if and only if all of their classical Ulm invariants, indexed by universe-zero ordinals, agree.
informal.UlmsTheorem.iso_of_ulm_invariants: Equal Ulm invariants at every universe-zero ordinal imply an additive equivalence between countable reduced abelian p-groups, via finite height-preserving partial isomorphisms and a back-and-forth limit.
informal.UlmsTheorem.ulmInvariant_iso_invariant: An additive equivalence preserves every classical Ulm invariant.
informal.UlmsTheorem.UlmDifferentialRegression.no: The groups Z/4 x Z/4 and Z/2 x Z/8 are not additively isomorphic; the proof exercises the classification theorem and independently detects their different zeroth Ulm invariants.

records.title: Unconditional Schauder Bases
records.abstract: Develops an API for Schauder bases and unconditional Schauder bases of complete normed spaces, including ordered partial-sum convergence, rearrangement criteria for unconditionality, and an arbitrary-index variant built on unconditional summability, then proves a finite sign criterion: a family with dense closed span, nonzero vectors, and a uniform finite sign bound is the basis of an unconditional Schauder basis.

informal.UnconditionalCriterion.exists_unconditio: Finite sign criterion for sequences: if `x : ℕ → E` has dense closed linear span, every `x n` is nonzero, and finite sign changes are uniformly bounded by `C`, then `x` is the basis sequence of an unconditional Schauder basis.

Abstract-index form of the finite sign criterion: under the same dense span, nonzero, and uniform finite sign bound hypotheses for an arbitrarily indexed family, there is an abstractly indexed unconditional Schauder basis whose basis family is exactly `x`.

records.title: Virasoro Project
records.abstract: Formalizes the Virasoro algebra, its Witt-algebra central extension, Verma modules, and the basic bosonic Sugawara construction.

informal.VirasoroProject.VirasoroAlgebra: Defines the Virasoro algebra as a one-dimensional central extension of the Witt algebra.
informal.VirasoroProject.sugawaraRepresentation: Constructs the basic bosonic Sugawara representation of the Virasoro algebra from locally truncated Heisenberg actions.

records.title: Mean-field derivation and well-posedness of the Vlasov equation
records.abstract: Formalizes the mean-field limit, Dobrushin stability, and forward-in-time well-posedness for the Vlasov equation via Wasserstein-1 optimal transport.

informal.Vlasov.vlasovWellPosedness: Forward-in-time existence of a Lagrangian solution to the Vlasov equation on any finite horizon, for interaction forces that are Lipschitz gradients of an even pair potential (class AssW) — with no smallness restriction on the Lipschitz constant.
informal.Vlasov.dobrushin: A Wasserstein-1 form of Dobrushin's 1979 stability estimate (the original uses a truncated metric) - two Lagrangian Vlasov solutions with finite first moments at every time separate at most at an exponential Gronwall rate.
informal.Vlasov.meanFieldLimit: Conditional mean-field limit - given Wasserstein-1 convergence of the initial empirical data and a uniform Dobrushin stability estimate for the empirical curves, the N-particle empirical measures converge to the Vlasov solution uniformly on any finite horizon.
informal.Vlasov.weak_isLagrangianVlasovSolutionOn: On a time window with L * T^2 < 1, a weak solution with the standing regularity (even C^2 pair potential AssW2, finite first moments, narrow continuity, time-continuity of the convolution force at each point, continuity of the convolution-derivative field, and a uniform spatial first-moment bound on the window) is Lagrangian - the pushforward of its initial datum along the characteristic flow.

records.title: Whitehead's theorem for CW-complexes
records.abstract: Formalizes Whitehead's theorem — a continuous map between CW-complexes that induces isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence — including the supporting theory of CW-complexes, relative homotopy groups, the homotopy extension property, and compression of maps.

informal.WhiteheadTheorem: Proves that a continuous map between CW-complexes inducing isomorphisms on all homotopy groups is a homotopy equivalence.

records.title: Thakur's hypotheses on power sums of F_q[t]
records.abstract: Formalizes four components of Thakur's hypotheses on power sums over finite polynomial rings, including uniqueness and monotonicity results for the carry-free digit optimization problems and the Laurent-series expansion of finite-field power sums.

informal.ZetaH123.H1.main_theorem: Proves uniqueness of the admissible base-q decomposition maximizing the H1 power-sum weight functional.
informal.ZetaH123.H2.main: Proves the H2 unique-minimizer statement for the recursive digit/carry-free optimization problem defining the values s_d(k).
informal.ZetaH123.H3.main_theorem: Proves the H3 monotonicity statement that s_d(k) is strictly less than s_d(k+1) when p does not divide k.
informal.ZetaH123.Lem41.main: Proves the Lemma 4.1 Laurent-series expansion for S_d(k), with nonzero coefficients indexed by the carry-free tuples.

records.title: Simple zeros of the Riemann zeta function
records.abstract: Formalizes Lamzouri's Hilbert-space proof of lower bounds for simple and distinct zeros of the Riemann zeta function. From explicit Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation hypotheses, the development proves that eventually more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeros are simple and on the critical line and more than 83.625% are distinct. It includes the finite-multiset Hilbert-space inequality, zeta-zero multiplicity symmetries, an admissible cutoff construction, and certified trigonometric estimates.

informal.ZetaZeros.simple_proportion_d4: Assuming the stated Riemann--von Mangoldt and unconditional pair-correlation formulas, beyond some height more than 67.25% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and lie on the critical line.
informal.ZetaZeros.distinct_proportion_d5: Under the same two explicit analytic hypotheses, beyond some height more than 83.625% of nontrivial zeta zeros are distinct.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_simpleRealPart_lower: Bounds from below the number of multiplicity-one real points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the squared test-kernel sum of any admissible function.
informal.ZetaZeros.card_lower: Bounds from below the number of distinct points in a finite nonempty conjugation-invariant multiset using the same Hilbert-space kernel method.

records.title: Irrationality of ζ(3)
records.abstract: Formalizes Beukers' proof of Apéry's theorem for ζ(3), including the integral identities, denominator estimates, positivity, upper bounds, and final irrationality contradiction.

informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.linear_int: Clears denominators in the Apéry integral to produce a linear form in 1 and ζ(3).
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_pos: Proves positivity of the transformed Beukers-Apéry integral.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.JJ_upper: Bounds the Beukers-Apéry integral by a geometric factor times the ζ(3) series.
informal.LeanPool.Zeta3Irrational.fun1_tendsto_ze: Shows that the denominator-cleared Apéry linear forms tend to zero.

records.title: ZFLean
records.abstract: Develops a practical ZFC set-theory framework with von Neumann naturals, integers, rationals, functions, embeddings, isomorphisms, booleans, and sums.

informal.ZFSet.isIso_of_biembedding: Proves a Cantor-Bernstein theorem for ZF sets.
informal.ZFSet.ZFNat.induction: Provides induction for the von Neumann natural numbers.
informal.ZFSet.ZFInt.induction: Provides induction for the quotient construction of ZF integers.

records.title: The Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon information inequality
records.abstract: Formalizes the Zhang-Yeung inequality, the first known non-Shannon-type entropy inequality, together with its dual and averaged forms derived through the copy lemma.

informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung: Proves the Zhang-Yeung non-Shannon-type information inequality for four discrete random variables.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_dual: Proves the dual form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.
informal.ZhangYeung.zhangYeung_averaged: Proves the averaged symmetric form of the Zhang-Yeung inequality.

records.title: kim-em/erdos-unit-distance-comparator
records.abstract: Comparator wrapper certifying that the ErdosUnitDistance library proves the literal negation of the uniform-constant form of Erdős's unit-distance conjecture, from a Mathlib-only statement of that negation.

records.title: teorth/sendov
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Sendov's conjecture, and of its Phelps-Rodriguez strengthening, in full generality: if every zero of a complex polynomial p of degree n >= 2 lies in the closed unit disk, then every zero a of p has a critical point of p within distance 1 of it, and within distance strictly less than 1 unless |a| = 1 and p is a scalar multiple of z^n - a^n. The proof is by contradiction. Degrees 2 to 4 fall to an elementary integral computation; degree 5 upward goes through two estimates on the same integral -- a polar channel and an origin channel -- which are shown to be incompatible, reducing the theorem to a single numerical inequality. That inequality is discharged by exact rational Bernstein certificates, generated outside Lean and re-verified inside it, in both of its ranges: per-degree certificates for 5 <= n <= 100, and, for n >= 101, a single degree-58 certificate closing the one-variable inequality that the analytic large-degree reduction leaves behind. The boundary case |a| = 1 is proved separately from a reciprocal identity, and it is there that the equality classification is extracted. Nothing here is claimed to be new: the informal proof being formalized is a digestion of Lech Mazur's proof, which had already been formalized in Lean, so this is a second and independently checkable machine-checked proof of Sendov's conjecture, whose additional content is the Phelps-Rodriguez equality case. The Lean source was written by an AI agent under the direction and review of the author. There is no sorry outside the two deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and no floating point in any statement or proof.

records.title: LionSR/LDT-comparator
records.abstract: This project formalizes the main soundness theorem for the quantum low individual degree test. It proves that a projective two-prover strategy which passes the test admits polynomial measurements that are consistent with one another and with the provers' point measurements, with an explicit error bound.

records.title: AxiomMath/PrimeGapsLib
records.abstract: `PrimeGapsLib` is an evolving codebase aimed at housing results about gaps in primes. The flagship result thus far is that pairs of primes are separated by at most 246 infinitely often, conditional on the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem. The 246 proof was generated collaboratively between human formalisers at Axiom Math and AxiomProver, their in-house theorem proving system. Community feedback and contributions are welcome!

records.title: xinjiegit/ben_27_formalization
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof that there are absolute constants c > 0 and p₀ such that, for every prime p ≥ p₀, the minimum size m(p) of a set A ⊆ 𝔽_p with |A| ≥ 2 and no uniquely represented sum satisfies m(p) ≥ c (log p / log log p)².  Here representations are unordered two-element multisets from A, repeated summands are allowed, and "no unique sum" means that every such multiset has a distinct equal-sum mate.

records.title: rkirov/jordan_pick
records.abstract: The Jordan curve theorem, formalized in Lean 4 against Mathlib: a continuous injective map from the circle into the plane has a complement with exactly two connected components. The hypothesis is bare continuity and injectivity — no smoothness, piecewise-linearity or rectifiability — which is what makes the theorem hard and what separates it from the polygonal case. The proof follows Maehara's reduction to the Brouwer fixed point theorem, via a crossing lemma for transversal paths in a rectangle and the fact that every component has the curve as its boundary, together with a farthest-pair normalization that pins down exactly one bounded component. Because Mathlib has no Brouwer fixed point theorem at the pinned revision, Brouwer is built here from the ground up: covering-space path lifting for the circle giving π₁(S¹) ≅ ℤ, then no-retraction of the disk onto its boundary, then Brouwer on the disk by ray-retraction, then the general nonempty-compact-convex case by nearest-point projection. The statement is expressed in Mathlib's own vocabulary. The proof is sorry-free and depends on Lean's three standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) and nothing else.

records.title: elliotglazer/erdos501
records.abstract: Erdős problem #501 (Erdős 1961; Erdős–Hajnal 1971, Problem 38): for every real x let A_x be a bounded set of reals of Lebesgue outer measure < 1; must there be an infinite independent set, i.e. an infinite X ⊆ ℝ with x ∉ A_y for all distinct x, y ∈ X?  And if the sets A_x are closed of measure < 1, must there be an independent set of size 3?  This repository formalizes both answers.  Second question: yes — closed sets of measure < 1 admit an infinite independent set (Newelski–Pawlikowski–Seredyński 1987; no boundedness is needed), hence one of size 3.  First question: independent of ZFC.  Under CH (as ℵ₁ = 𝔠) Hechler's 1972 construction gives a family of bounded sets of outer measure < 1 (in fact countable and null) with no infinite independent set — a Mathlib-level theorem — and the negation of the first question holds in the Boolean-valued model of the collapse algebra Col(ω₁, 𝒫(ω)); after adding 𝔠⁺ random reals (Glazer and Sol 2026, adapting the paper's ω₂ random reals over a CH ground) the first question has a positive answer, so it holds in the Boolean-valued model of the random algebra with 𝔠⁺ coordinates.  Both Boolean-valued models are built in a Lean 4 port of Han–van Doorn's Flypitch (the framework of their independence-of-CH proof), and Flypitch's completeness theorem turns them into two-valued models.  The comparator challenge states the results in Mathlib alone: the language of set theory, the theory ZFC (Flypitch's axiomatization: extensionality, empty set, ordered pairs, union, power set, infinity, regularity, Zorn's lemma, strong collection) and the sentence Erdos501 ("every complete ordered field has the Erdős property") are defined in Mathlib's ModelTheory, and independence is stated semantically as ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ Erdos501) ∧ ¬ (ZFC ⊨ᵇ ∼Erdos501); a faithfulness theorem shows that in Mathlib's ZFSet the sentence is equivalent to the Mathlib statement of the first question, verbatim the proposition of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures.  All targets are proved from propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.  As far as we know this is the first Erdős problem whose resolution is a formally verified independence result.

records.title: A proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture, formalized
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the Regts–Sevenster conjecture. A complex-valued graph parameter, normalized at the empty graph and invariant under isomorphism, has exponentially bounded edge-connection rank if and only if it is a mixed partition function. For a natural rank base R, a representing model can be chosen with k even and 2ℓ odd colours satisfying k + 2ℓ ≤ R. The development also proves the even connection-rank growth limit, minimum total colour dimension, minimal parity formulas and prescribed-dimension criterion. Schrijver's factorial argument supplies nilpotent-trace vanishing; semisimplicity and Deligne's fibre-functor theorem give the model; a polynomial commutant estimate gives the sharp colour budget. Deligne's theorem and the required symmetric-group character theory are proved within the development. The appendix's trace-zeta results give rationality and degree bounds, with an independent proof of nilpotent-trace vanishing. The theorems of record use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, checked by pinned audits.

records.title: vo-rodrigues/wallace-problem-palomar
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the theorem that every torsion-free Abelian group of cardinality continuum admits a Hausdorff countably compact group topology in which every convergent sequence is eventually constant, and constructs a commutative Tychonoff countably compact cancellative topological monoid that is not a group, giving a negative answer to Wallace's question.

records.title: dcposch/jc2-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem A (ODE rigidity, all weights; label thm:ode, Theorem 6.1 in the current compilation of the campaign paper): if polynomials A, C over an integral domain of characteristic zero and an integer weight nu >= 1 satisfy A*C' - nu*A'*C = c for a nonzero constant c, then deg A <= 1 (TheoremA).  Also a standalone positive-characteristic strengthening extracted from the same proof (TheoremA_charP): the same conclusion over a domain of characteristic p under the degree bounds nu*deg A < p and deg C < p.  The theorem is the rigidity engine of the depth-two block analysis in the campaign on the plane Jacobian problem at Newton-degree pair (72,108).

records.title: stalex444/arithmetic-of-time
records.abstract: A kernel-checked chirality package for the Padovan substitution (0 ↦ 1, 1 ↦ 2, 2 ↦ 01 on Fin 3; its incidence matrix has characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1, an orientation fact that is not used or compared). Three compared theorems, all at the iterate-factor level — they quantify over factors of the concrete words S^[n] [x], never over an abstract subshift. (1) The successor invariant: in every positive iterate from any seed, the letter 0 ("a") is immediately followed by 1 ("b"). (2) Chirality: the word 20 ("ca") is a factor of an iterate while its reversal 02 ("ac") is a factor of no iterate from any seed — the factor language reads differently backwards — proved from the invariant, with no enumeration on the ac side. (3) No palindromic factor: no factor of length ≥ 4 of any iterate from any seed (including the zeroth iterate) is a palindrome, via a complete length-≤5 window certificate for the seed a together with the index shift S [0] = [1], S [1] = [2], which exhibits every seed's iterate as a seed-a iterate.

records.title: stalex444/pdt-lean
records.abstract: Kernel-checked exact-constant results for the CHSH operator T = A₀B₀ + A₀B₁ + A₁B₀ − A₁B₁ of an arbitrary CHSH tuple (Mathlib's IsCHSHTuple: self-adjoint involutions with the A's commuting with the B's). (1) The Landau identity: in any *-ring, T² = 4 + [A₀,A₁]·[B₁,B₀] — the exact, representation-independent correction to the naive T² = 8·1 (chsh_mul_self). (2) Tsirelson's bound in norm form: ‖T‖ ≤ 2√2 for every CHSH tuple in every nontrivial unital real C*-normed algebra (chsh_norm_le). (3) The classical constant, exactly: if either party's pair commutes, ‖T‖ = 2 — not merely ≤ 2 (chsh_norm_of_comm). (4) Necessity of noncommutativity: any violation ‖T‖ > 2 forces A₀A₁ ≠ A₁A₀ and B₀B₁ ≠ B₁B₀ — noncommutativity within both parties is necessary for any violation of the classical bound (noncomm_of_chsh_norm_gt_two). (5) The exact constant of M₄(ℝ): in the l2 operator norm, 2√2 is the greatest element of the set of CHSH operator norms over 4×4 real matrices — an upper bound for every tuple, attained by an explicit real-Pauli tuple (chsh_opNorm_isGreatest), so the maximal violation 2√2 is possible, not just bounded. The witness side stays compared: the explicit quadruple is verified to be a genuine CHSH tuple, its CHSH operator has eigenvalue exactly 2√2 on the explicit nonzero vector (1,0,0,1) and l2 operator norm exactly 2√2; the ordered star-ring bounds T ≤ (2√2)·1 and (commutative case) T ≤ 2 and the strict gap 2 < 2√2 complete the picture. A falsification is compared alongside: the saturating tuple's T² is not c·1 for ANY real c (chsh_sq_ne quantifies over every scalar), so the scalar-square route to the norm is closed for every scalar; the norm results here go through the C*-identity (and, for the generic bound, the Landau identity) instead.

records.title: dcposch/jc2-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the vertex-gap obstruction at (k,d2) = (2,2) (label thm:22, Theorem 3.4 in the current compilation) from the campaign paper "A Vertex-Gap Obstruction for Low-Degree Strip Pairs in the Plane Jacobian Conjecture": for polynomials P, Q in K[x,y] over a field K of characteristic not in {2,3,5}, supported in the normalized type-(2,2) Newton strips along (1,2) with [P,Q] = x^2, the block coefficients satisfy a3 = 0 and a2^2*a6 = 0 - so the generic chart a2*a6 != 0 of the strip family is empty (VertexGap22, plus the side-symmetric companion VertexGap22_swapped in the mirrored labels). Also formalized: the arithmetic corner-enumeration lemma behind the vertex normalization (lem:enum, Lemma 2.2; CornerEnumeration) and the side-symmetric form of the gap condition, hypothesis (ii) as corrected by the erratum recorded in Section 8 (GapConditionSideSymm).  The theorem is the mechanism that empties the generic chart of the (8,28) strip subcase in the campaign on the plane Jacobian problem at Newton-degree pair (72,108).

records.title: yuanchenyang/lean_low_rank_univariate_sos
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of Legat, Yuan and Parrilo, "Low-Rank Univariate Sum of Squares Has No Spurious Local Minima" (SIAM J. Optim. 33(3), 2023). For a real univariate polynomial p and a pair of polynomials u = (u₁, u₂), consider the quadratically penalized Burer–Monteiro objective f_p(u) = ‖σ(u) - p‖² with σ(u) = u₁² + u₂², the norm coming from any inner product on ℝ[x]. The formalized theorem states that if p is a sum of two squares (which is the case for any nonnegative  univariate polynomial) and u is a second-order critical point of f_p (vanishing gradient and positive semidefinite Hessian, Definition 3.1 of the paper), then σ(u) = p, equivalently f_p(u) = 0; hence every SOCP, and in particular every local minimum, is a global minimum. The development follows the paper's proof: the gcd decomposition u = a·u₀ with u₀ coprime, the observation that σ(u₀) has no real roots, a Bézout-based "hgroup" lemma writing a sum of squares p as g·q + s·σ(u₀) with s a sum of squares when g and σ(u₀) are coprime, the factor-peeling argument that replaces the quadratic factors of a shared with σ(u₀) by X², and the final certificate argument combining the first- and second-order conditions.

records.title: catskillsresearch/cardb
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of an exact enumeration identity and two consequences: for a finite type α, the number of families B ⊆ Set α that are topological bases equals the sum, over all topologies τ on α, of 2^(|τ| − |M_τ|), where M_τ is the canonical minimal basis of minimal open neighbourhoods (Mathlib's nhdsKer {x} at each point). Kernel-reducible enumeration gives the exact table #(0)=2, #(1)=2, #(2)=10, #(3)=142. A quantitative sandwich then shows that the discrete fiber 2^(2^N − N) dominates: for N ≥ 2 the remaining fibers contribute at most 2^(N(N−1) + 3·2^(N−2)), the ratio to the discrete term tends to 1, and for N ≥ 10 the total is at most twice the discrete term. The argument is a fiber decomposition: every finite topology is Alexandrov-discrete, the minimal neighbourhoods generate it, and the bases generating τ are exactly the families B with M_τ ⊆ B ⊆ {U | τ.IsOpen U}. The informal account is the companion note CARDB.md in this repository. The Lean source was written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.

records.title: guanyangwang/ktv-swap-lean-comparator
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization and Comparator verification of the spectral-gap theorem for the lazy swap chain on binary contingency tables with fixed margins.

records.title: google-deepmind/formal-conjectures
records.abstract: Formal proof of the First Cuboid Conjecture, which states that for all positive coprime integers a, b with a ≠ b, a certain degree-8 polynomial P_{a,b}(t) over ℤ is irreducible. This conjecture was proposed by Shapirov in "Perfect cuboids and irreducible polynomials" (arXiv:1108.5348) as part of a family of three conjectures whose combined truth would imply the nonexistence of a perfect Euler brick. The proof first analyses rational factors and the symmetry F(−x) vs F(x) to reduce irreducibility of the degree-8 polynomial to irreducibility of a degree-4 factor Q_{a,b}, and the coprime branch to a Diophantine identity. Irreducibility of Q is in turn reduced to the quartic Diophantine equation x⁴ + 34x²y² + y⁴ = z², whose only trivial solutions are established by Fermat-style infinite descent. The formal proof was autonomously discovered by the AlphaProof Nexus agent; an independent informal proof using rank-zero elliptic curves was given by Asiryan (arXiv:2510.11768).

records.title: rwst/Even-Integral
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which improves on a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. At α = 3/2 this is Mahler's question, and open; his Problem 5 asks whether 𝒮 has an element greater than 2. This formalization decides 𝒮 versus 𝒵 for every quadratic Pisot number: the golden mean is the only one in 𝒮, so none greater than 2 lies there and Problem 5 loses its whole natural class of candidates, though the problem itself stays open. The case that had resisted the source paper's four constructions is α = 1 + √2, settled by an exact computation rather than an estimate: with ξ = (2−√2)/4 one has ⌊ξ(1+√2)^(n+1)⌋ = Pₙ − [n odd] for the Pell numbers P, so every integral part is even. The mechanism generalizes: for a real quadratic pair with second conjugate in (−1,0), the closed-form multiplier ξ = −β/(α−β) makes m divide ⌊ξαⁿ⌋ for every n ≥ 0 whenever m ∣ a and m ∣ b−1 — an exact congruence, not a confinement of fractional parts — and all but finitely many of those integral parts are then composite. The informal account is the companion paper doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.20582.79689. Credit divides as follows, in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematical discovery and the formalization are the AI agent's; the agent also drafted the prose of the companion paper, which the author revised; the direction and the review are the author's, who is responsible for the mathematical content. Bibliographic authorship of the paper is the author's alone — the agent is credited in its Acknowledgements, not in its byline, as is usual for an AI tool. There is no sorry outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.

records.title: Vulkin-prog/paper-c-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of a quantitative Poisson approximation for the starting points of long constant stretches of an extended Rademacher random completely multiplicative function in a dyadic block. The compared theorem uses a finite prime-sign cylinder and proves, uniformly in the critical window |L - log_2 N| <= C, that the total-variation distance to Pois(N/2^L) is O_C((log log N)^-2). It is conditional on three fully stated ordinary propositions specialized from Arratia--Goldstein--Gordon, Evertse--Silverman, and Nicolas--Robin; those propositions are theorem arguments, not Lean axioms.

records.title: benkeene/erdos266
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the Kovač–Tao resolution of Erdős problem #266 (a conjecture of Stolarsky): it is not true that every sequence of positive integers with convergent reciprocal sum admits an integer shift t >= 1 making the shifted Ahmes series irrational.  The stronger construction is also formalized: a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers whose shifted series has a rational sum for every admissible rational shift.

records.title: sloisel/MPE-Formal
records.abstract: Machine-checked proofs of three probabilistic convergence theorems for restarted Minimal Polynomial Extrapolation (MPE) applied to nonlinear fixed-point iterations.  Dithered restarts keep the error below the doubly exponential schedule delta^(theta^m), for any theta in (1,2), from every starting point -- the breakdown set included -- with an explicit failure-probability exponent over the dither; in the root sense the convergence order is at least theta.  Under simple spectrum, the error follows a quadratically shrinking dither schedule (root order at least 2) with failure probability linear in the initial radius up to a logarithmic factor, and MPE coincides with Reduced Rank Extrapolation at every cycle. With no dither at all, the restarted iteration from a single uniformly random starting point at worst squares the error at every cycle with high probability, under two checkable hypotheses on the Jacobian and the quadratic Taylor coefficients.  The registered statements are self-contained over mathlib: every object of the construction is introduced by an explicit defining equation among the hypotheses.

records.title: ehrlich-b/sequential-products-lean
records.abstract:
A sequential product on the effects of an order-unit space is a binary operation a & b, read "first test a, then test b with the state updated by the first test", satisfying the seven axioms S1-S7 of van de Wetering (arXiv:1803.11139, Definition 2). This development registers two classification theorems for such products on the Hermitian matrix algebras.
On H_N(R), the Hermitian N x N real matrices with N >= 1, every sequential product is the Lueders product sqrt(a) b sqrt(a): there is no free parameter. On H_N(C) with N >= 3, every sequential product has the twist normal form a^(1/2+it) b a^(1/2-it) for a unique real t. The twist family is a one-parameter deformation of the Lueders product, and the complex theorem says nothing outside it satisfies the axioms. The equations are asserted on all effects, including singular ones, and the uniqueness of t is part of the registered statement.
Direction. Both registered classification theorems are necessity: a product satisfying the axioms is supplied, and the theorem says it has the stated normal form. The two converses differ in status and neither is registered. For the complex case, that each real t defines a SeqProd satisfying S2 is proved in the wider development; together with the registered uniqueness it is what would make the parameter map injective. For the real case, that the Lueders formula defines a SeqProd satisfying S2 is not proved anywhere in this development. Nothing here registers a bijection between parameters and products, or the admissibility of the Lueders formula.
The package also registers two classical theorems the development proves in passing. Albert's power-associativity theorem: in a commutative Jordan ring carrying an R-module structure, x^(m+1) * x^(n+1) = x^(m+n+2), with no unit, finite dimension, formal reality or positivity assumed. And the real case of Wigner's theorem: every transition probability preserving self-map of the rays of a finite-dimensional real inner product space is induced by a linear isometry, with bijectivity not assumed but derived.
Both classification theorems are proved from S1-S7 with no hypotheses beyond the dimension bounds, and their axiom closures contain only Lean's three core axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The continuity axiom S2 is stated in the order-unit norm, as an explicit epsilon-delta condition, so the statement file depends on no normed-space or topological instance; the equivalence with continuity in the carrier's Frobenius topology is proved in the development.
Scope. Comparator registers four theorems across three separate entries: the two sequential-product classifications above, which use the SeqProd interface and the axiom S2 and correspond to numbered rows of the manuscript; and the two ancillary classical theorems, Albert and Wigner, which use neither and correspond to no manuscript row. Nothing beyond those four registered theorems is claimed by this submission.
The two classification theorems are two rows of a thirty-six row manifest tracking the numbered results of the accompanying manuscript. The manuscript as a whole is not formalized: as of 2026-08-12 the manifest stands at 12 rows formalized, 19 partial, and 5 absent. In particular the quaternionic row H_n(H) and the Albert-algebra row H_3(O) of the manuscript's main theorem are not proved here, and the coalescence and diagonal-homomorphism lemmas are established on the concrete carrier H_N(C) rather than at the manuscript's stated generality of a finite-dimensional simple Euclidean Jordan algebra.

records.title: teal-sea/zeta-lab
records.abstract: A variational identity for the Fredholm operator A = I + T on the interval I = [-1/2, 1/2], where T is convolution against the Farmer-Gonek-Lee pair-correlation form factor F1(x) = |x| - 4x^2 + sum_k a_k |x|^(2k+3) with a_k = 2^(2k+3) k! / (2k+2)!. Let w = A^(-1)1 and c* = <1, A^(-1)1>. Over the source-admissible class of scalar profiles v(s) = phi(Ls)^2 induced by even, radially nonincreasing C^2 windows supported exactly on [-L/2, L/2] with 0 <= phi <= 1 and uniform L^1 bounds on phi'' and (phi^2)'', the supremum of <1,v>^2 / <Av,v> equals c*, and the infimum of the reciprocal quotient <Av,v> / <1,v>^2 equals 1/c*. The upper bound <1,v>^2 <= c* <Av,v> is energy Cauchy-Schwarz. It holds for every v, it is classical, and it is not the content of this result. The content is the reverse inequality over the constrained class: c* is the value of the unconstrained variational problem, and the identity says that imposing evenness, radial monotonicity, an exact compact support, the amplitude ceiling 0 <= phi <= 1 and uniform L^1 bounds on the second derivatives does not lower the supremum. That direction is proved by exhibiting an explicit endpoint-tapered family inside the class, indexed by the scale L, whose quotient converges to c*. Both orientations are advertised because the orientation is load-bearing: it is the quotient with <1,v>^2 in the numerator whose supremum is c*, and the supporting development also proves that the two are not interchangeable. The advertised statement is existential in the profile and in the two uniform constants, so it carries its own non-vacuity: an IsLUB or IsGLB assertion over the image of an empty class is unsatisfiable in the reals, so the theorem cannot hold unless the class is populated by the constants for which it is stated. Audience. The kernel F1 is the pair-correlation form factor and the window class is the generalized, load-bearing class of Section 7.1 of the cited paper rather than a convenient flat-topped realization, so the constrained supremum settled here is the quantity that a critical-line proportion argument built on that framework optimizes; analytic number theorists working on the proportion of zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line, and on pair correlation of its zeros, are the audience for which the exact value of that supremum over the admissible class, rather than a bound on it, is the relevant fact. The statement is also a closure result for a constrained admissible class in the variational theory of Fredholm integral operators (MSC 45B05, 49R05) and can be read there without reference to its origin. What the theorem itself asserts is bounded by the scope field below: it is a statement about a Fredholm operator on an interval and a class of test profiles, and it is evidence for nothing beyond that.

records.title: lennrt/palomar-formalizations
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Lemma 7.1 and the outer-matrix content of Theorem 7.2 for generalized cubic subdivision. It defines the naturally indexed 28n by 28n outer matrix row-by-row from the authenticated released MATLAB masks, including all previous/current/next-sector references. records.title: teal-sea/zeta-lab
records.abstract: Davenport and Heilbronn (1936) exhibited a Dirichlet series with real coefficients satisfying a Riemann-type functional equation which nevertheless has zeros off the critical line. It is the standard demonstration that a functional equation of Riemann type does not on its own force the Riemann Hypothesis, it is the reference counterexample against which structural explanations of the Riemann Hypothesis are tested, and the location of its zeros remains an active subject. The function is DH(s) = (1 - i*kappa)/2 * L(s, chi) + (1 + i*kappa)/2 * L(s, chi^-1) for a quartic Dirichlet character chi mod 5 and kappa = (sqrt(10 - 2*sqrt 5) - 2)/(sqrt 5 - 1), the value that rotates the two conjugate root numbers onto each other and so makes the Dirichlet coefficients real. This submission advertises one theorem, the analytic half of the Davenport-Heilbronn theorem: there exists an entire function represented by the Davenport-Heilbronn Dirichlet series on Re z > 1 whose completion (pi/5)^(-(s+1)/2) * Gamma((s+1)/2) * f(s) is symmetric under s -> 1-s. The statement is existential in f, so it carries its own non-vacuity and needs none of the character theory used to construct the witness. What the work consists of. The Davenport-Heilbronn function is not a library object anywhere we could find, so the development builds it: the quartic character mod 5, the linear combination, entirety on all of C, the identification of the Dirichlet coefficients as the real period-5 sequence 1, kappa, -kappa, -1, 0, and the completed functional equation. The last of these is where the content sits. It reduces to a root-number identity whose convention-sensitive constants are derived inside the development, from Mathlib's Real.cos_pi_div_five by radical algebra, rather than transcribed from a table; the standard sources state kappa without deriving it in a form a kernel will accept, and getting it wrong yields a function whose coefficients are not real and which therefore is not the counterexample. The functional equation is stated with explicit guards excluding the poles of the two Gamma factors, because Mathlib's junk value Gamma = 0 at the poles would otherwise make the unrestricted equation false for reasons having nothing to do with the mathematics. Audience. The Davenport-Heilbronn function is a named object of analytic number theory with a continuing literature on its zeros, so a machine-checked construction of it is of direct interest to number theorists working on zeros of L-functions and on what a Riemann-type functional equation does and does not imply. It is also the object a formalized treatment of the Davenport-Heilbronn theorem has to have before it can say anything, and this supplies it in a form that carries its own non-vacuity. Prior art. A search of Mathlib at the revision pinned by this repository found no Davenport-Heilbronn function and no formalization of this functional equation. That is a bounded search of one library. No systematic search of other proof assistants or of the mathematical literature for prior formalizations has been run, and no novelty against the literature is claimed: the mathematics is Davenport and Heilbronn's, published in 1936. Scope. The Davenport-Heilbronn theorem itself is NOT proved here. Its full statement additionally requires a zero s with Re s different from 1/2, and that conjunct appears nowhere in the advertised theorem. What is offered is the analytic half alone. No numerical enclosure for any zero of DH is asserted, and nothing here is a statement about the Riemann zeta function or the Riemann Hypothesis.

records.title: williamjblair/lean-proofs
records.abstract: Machine-checked Lean 4 proofs of solved research problems from the Erdős problems collection, hosted as stable formal_proof targets for Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures. The principal result is an affirmative answer to Erdős Problem #730 (Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa and Straus, 1975): the set of pairs n < m for which binom(2n, n) and binom(2m, m) have the same set of prime divisors is infinite, and in fact contains infinitely many consecutive pairs (n, n + 1). The proof formalises the argument posted informally by Liam Price on the problem's discussion page on 24 June 2026: Kummer's theorem converts equality of prime supports into a base-p digit condition, an explicit quadratic family of consecutive pairs is constructed, a fixed-depth Fourier estimate bounds the digit obstruction on blocks of length p^r, a uniform depth tail uses a Mertens-type reciprocal-prime input, the top-prime range is handled by fixed-modulus divisor switching using the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions, and an exact rational density budget yields positive lower density and hence infinitude. The repository also proves the sumset form of Erdős Problem #154 (equidistribution of A + A in residue classes for Sidon sets A with |A| ~ sqrt N, from Lindström's theorem) and hosts smaller bounded results for Problems #94, #399 and #1074. Every tracked theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; each registry statement under Palomar/ restates its result in a Challenge importing Mathlib alone.

records.title: mbaccaro-dev/mathematical-proofs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the sequence-level conditioning construction for Selberg divisor feedback. Two explicit perturbations of the von Mangoldt weight stay in the positive prime-power cone, approximate the divisor data to an arbitrary tolerance through twice the observation scale, separate their summatory outputs at a near-linear power scale, and retain one uniform linear Selberg bound.

records.title: xiangyazi24/palomar-hahn-hecke-appell
records.abstract: A Lean 4 verification of the coefficientwise Kronecker partial-fraction identity and the general boundary-cleared Hickerson--Mortenson Hecke--Appell identity for f_{n,n+p,n}, for all positive integers n and p.

records.title: mbaccaro-dev/mathematical-proofs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of the global power-of-two balance connecting dyadic defect, block variation, and positive Möbius-logarithm prefix energy. Eventual nonnegativity on exactly those dyadic blocks gives an explicit all-endpoint cubic energy bound. With the stated weighted-squarefree remainder estimate, the formalization also recovers the sharp 6/pi^2 leading coefficient and retains the complete finite-prefix correction.

records.title: mbaccaro-dev/mathematical-proofs
records.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of a residual-or-unmatched barrier for local Möbius cancellation. At every sufficiently large fixed-band scale, either the permitted edge length reaches the retained-prime product or every member of an explicit squarefree prime-product family is unmatched. Chebyshev estimates give the exact binomial and factorial population bounds. The product scale also converts residual rank to its logarithmic threshold with the exact limiting constant.

records.title: ashebson/kinin-lean
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of all sixteen units of Mishnah Kinnim, with a machine-checked physical optimization theorem for the Koppel--Reiss reading of Kinnim 3:2. For any list of pair counts grouped by owner, the priest has already acted on exactly half of the mixed birds above and half below. A physical world records one action level for every individual bird of every owner. Lean proves that every such world is compatible, by permutation, with the fixed half-split action list. Counting valid birds directly from each owner's closed-pair quota, the theorem proves that the exact minimum over all physical apportionments is twice the complement of the largest attainable subset sum not exceeding half the total, and constructs an apportionment attaining it. The repository also covers all sixteen units, flight recurrences, and replacement-inventory covers.

records.title: adas1236/KaltonPeckPalomar
records.abstract:
We prove the following mod-2 identity for real symplectic Banach spaces:
  If $(X, \omega)$ is a real symplectic Banach space, and $T \in L(X)$ satisfies:
    (1) $I + T^+T$ is Fredholm
    (2) $I + T^2$ has finite rank
  Then
    $\rank(T^2 + I) \equiv \dim \ker (I + T^+T) \pmod 2$.
In the above, $T^+$ represents the symplectic adjoint. See our paper for more depth in definitions. This identity is applied to show that no hyperplane of the real Kalton-Peck space has a complex structure. We note that in our notation, a symplectic Banach space always assumes that the symplectic form \omega is a strong symplectic form. See our paper for more detail on the definitions.
We formalize:
 (1) The mod-2 identity for arbitrary real symplectic Banach spaces
 (2) An application of the identity to show that if $T \in L(Z_2)$ and $T^2 + I$ has finite rank, then $T^2 + I$ has even rank.
     Here, Z_2 is the real Kalton-Peck space.
 (3) The corollary that no hyperplane of the real Kalton-Peck space has a complex structure.

records.title: xiangyazi24/palomar-qseries-prime-coefficients
records.abstract: For an explicitly defined difference B of two signed cone theta series over Q(sqrt(5)), Lean proves a closed nonmultiplicativity witness and a complete prime-index classification. For every rational prime p congruent to 1 modulo 10, B((p-1)/10) is one of -2, -1, 1, 2; a norm-negative golden integer generator and its strict fundamental-window normalization exist; and the coefficient has magnitude two exactly when the resulting geometric residue invariant is one modulo three. The invariant is also proved independent of the generator within the explicitly defined signed fundamental-unit orbit.

records.title: CBirkbeck/uniform-sheafy-tate-domains-lean
records.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalisation of *Uniform sheafy Tate rings that are not stably uniform* (Birkbeck–Torzewski), answering Question 7 of Kedlaya's *Nonarchimedean Scottish Book* in the negative: a sheafy uniform Huber pair need not be stably uniform. Buzzard–Verberkmoes and Mihara proved that stably uniform Tate Huber rings are sheafy; whether the converse holds was open.
The paper gives two complete Tate algebras over a complete discretely valued field `k` that are uniform, nonnoetherian integral domains with `A° = A₀`, strongly sheafy (every Tate algebra `A⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩` is sheafy), and yet not stably uniform, because an explicit rational localisation is not uniform. The first (Theorem 1.1) is the finite-jet pinching algebra `𝓐 = B ×_D C`, the pullback of a Milnor square with `B = k⟨W, Q⟩/(Q²)`, `C = k⟨W, W⁻¹⟩⟨Q⟩`, `D = C/(Q²)` — concretely, the series in `k⟨W, W⁻¹⟩⟨Q⟩` whose `Q⁰`- and `Q¹`-coefficients have nonnegative `W`-support; its bad chart `𝓐⟨W/ϖ⟩ ≅ k⟨X, Q⟩/(Q²)` is non-reduced. The second (Theorem 8.1) is the weighted-parity algebra `𝒜_w`, whose bad chart is an integral domain; the paper proves it for every unbounded weight `w ≥ 1`, the formalisation for `w(n) = n`.
This submission certifies the seven conclusions of Theorem 1.1 together with two statements ruling out a vacuous reading of its sheafiness claims, stated self-containedly on Mathlib in `Challenge.lean` over an arbitrary complete ultrametric field with DVR valuation ring; Theorem 8.1 is certified by the repository's in-library configuration. The repository also develops the surrounding theory after Wedhorn's *Adic Spaces*: Huber and Tate rings, the adic spectrum, rational localisations, the structure presheaf, and sheafiness (Definition 8.26), including the strongly noetherian theorem (8.28(b)).

records.title: geoconuk/lean-misc-math
records.abstract: For a fixed angular radius theta in (0, pi/2), the least number M(n, theta) of spherical caps of angular radius theta, centred at points of the unit sphere of R^n, whose union is that whole sphere satisfies (1/n) log M(n, theta) -> -log sin theta as n -> infinity. This is the covering half of Wyner (1967): the elementary volume bound gives the lower bound on the covering number and a random-covering argument gives the upper bound. The statement is given in Mathlib's own vocabulary, as an asymptotic for Metric.coveringNumber of Metric.sphere 0 1 in EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) at chordal radius 2 sin (theta/2), and introduces no definition of its own; two compared lemmas establish that an angular cap of half-angle theta about a unit vector is exactly the closed chordal ball of that radius, which is what licenses reading the result as a statement about caps. Two further compared theorems rule out the junk values that the N-infinity-valued covering number and the logarithm would otherwise admit.

records.title: rwst/Square-Roots
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which answers a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. At α = 3/2 this is Mahler's question, and open; his Problem 3 asks whether √3 lies in 𝒮 or in 𝒵. This formalization settles that question and the whole square-root slice: √3 ∈ 𝒵 by an explicit ξ = 1.34160899796…, and for an integer m ≥ 2 one has √m ∈ 𝒮 exactly when m = 2. The cells √5, √6, √7, √8 put four explicit points of 𝒵 in the interval (2,3), the only interval where an answer to Dubickas's Problem 5 could live; they are formalized (SZ.exists_mem_MahlerZ_Ioo_two_three) but are not separately compared, being subsumed by the compared Theorem B. The mechanism is not Diophantine approximation but the arithmetic of Cantor sets, and rests on the triviality that √m² = m is an integer: splitting n into even and odd values turns the one orbit into two base-m orbits coupled by x + √m y = σ, and a covering induction — Utz's 1951 theorem on the distance set of the Cantor discontinuum at m = 3, proved here for every base and every modulus — solves that equation inside the restricted-digit set. The same machinery at a general modulus gives, for p ≥ 2 and non-square m ≥ 3 in either of two explicit ranges, a real ξ ≠ 0 with p ∣ ⌊ξ√mⁿ⌋ for every n ≥ 1, hence integral parts that are composite from some point on; and the greedy's branching shows the witnesses for √3 have cardinality 2^ℵ₀, so all but countably many of them are transcendental. The informal account is the companion paper doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.32215.43682. Credit divides as follows, in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematical discovery is the Fable-5 agent's; the formalization is the Fable-5 and Opus-5 agents'; the agents also drafted the prose of the companion paper, which the author revised; the direction and the review are the author's, who is responsible for the mathematical content. Bibliographic authorship of the paper is the author's alone — the collaboration is credited in its Acknowledgements, not in its byline, as is usual for an AI tool. There is no sorry outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency of the development itself.

records.title: novou/square-maximality-palomar
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of square maximality for spanning trees of induced subgraphs of the square lattice. For every positive integer n and every finite set S of n^2 points in Z^2, the induced lattice graph on S has at most as many spanning trees as the n by n square, with equality exactly when S is a translate of that square. The development also proves the corresponding strict and equality statements for arbitrary spanning subgraphs, together with the finite Matrix--Tree theorem and the proof chain used by the paper.

records.title: DiarHaidary/Nelson-Nguyen-conjecture-upper-bound-palomar
records.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of three sparse oblivious-subspace-embedding results at the Nelson--Nguyen parameter scale: the fully independent signed-hash SparseStack construction, independent uniform signed exact-s columns, and a limited-independence transfer for finite laws whose combined hash-sign selector marginals agree with SparseStack through order 4q.  At the stated rounded parameters the selected theorems give failure probability at most delta, with explicit strict bounds s < 1356 q / epsilon and m < 306456 (d + q) / epsilon^2 where those parameter conclusions are packaged.  The formalization is machine checked but has not been peer reviewed and makes no priority claim.

records.title: ehrlich-b/euclidean-jordan
records.abstract:
A Euclidean Jordan algebra is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space carrying a commutative bilinear product with a unit, satisfying the Jordan identity (x*y)*(x*x) = x*(y*(x*x)) and the associativity of the inner product <x*y, z> = <y, x*z>. This is Faraut-Koranyi's definition (Analysis on Symmetric Cones, III.1). This development formalizes the classical structure theory of these algebras.
Mathlib carries the Jordan identity as the typeclass IsCommJordan together with five operator-commutation lemmas, and nothing beyond that: no idempotent theory, no Peirce decomposition, no spectral theory. This development supplies that layer.
The registered results, in four separate Comparator configurations. (1) The Koecher / Alfsen-Shultz theorem: a unital linear order isomorphism of a Euclidean Jordan algebra is a Jordan automorphism, with the cone taken to be the sums-of-squares cone and the product carried as a bundled bilinear map so that the statement needs no ring instance to elaborate. (2) The single-element spectral theorem: every element of a finite-dimensional formally real Jordan algebra is a real linear combination of a complete family of pairwise-orthogonal idempotents. Finite-dimensionality is load-bearing rather than decorative - the polynomial algebra R[X] satisfies every other hypothesis and has no nonconstant spectral resolution. (3) The Jordan trace form tau(x,y) = tr(L_{x*y}): symmetric, associative, and positive definite, constructed from the multiplication alone rather than assumed. Symmetry and associativity are registered at their honest generality, which does not include finite-dimensionality; positive definiteness needs the spectral theorem and therefore does. (4) The frame Peirce decomposition: for a Jordan frame p_1, ..., p_n the algebra is the internal direct sum of the blocks V_ij over unordered pairs, together with the Faraut-Koranyi table entry dim V_ii = 1.
Direction and scope. Every registered theorem is proved outright from the stated hypotheses; none is conditional on a cited result. The development also proves, but does not register here, Albert's power-associativity theorem (x^(m+1) * x^(n+1) = x^(m+n+2), with no unit, finite dimension, formal reality or positivity assumed), which is registered from a separate development of the author's and is deliberately not re-registered; the existence of a Jordan frame in any nontrivial finite-dimensional Euclidean Jordan algebra; the associativity of the subalgebra generated by a single element; the Peirce subalgebras J_2(c) and J_0(c) as Euclidean Jordan algebras in their own right; and an order-unit-space structure with the sums-of-squares cone, proved to coincide with the Loewner order on the concrete carrier.
What is NOT here. Coordinatization is absent: the Jordan-von Neumann-Wigner route continues by making the off-diagonal block a composition algebra and applying Hurwitz's theorem to land J = H_n(K), and that step depends on the composition-algebra classification, which lives in a separate repository. This development therefore stops at the connectors and the frame-block structure. There is no functional calculus on the spectral resolution. Frame conjugacy (Faraut-Koranyi IV.2.5) is not proved - the development sidesteps it by carrying a Jordan frame as data rather than reasoning about the rank as a number. The classification of simple Euclidean Jordan algebras is not proved, and no statement about the exceptional algebra H_3(O) appears. Formal reality and the associativity of the inner product are equivalent over R in finite dimension, but that equivalence is not formalized, so both appear as hypotheses.
The abstract theory has a live carrier: H_n(K) for K = R or C, the Hermitian matrices under A*B = (AB+BA)/2, is an instance of the EuclideanJordanAlgebra class, checked by instance synthesis in the mechanical audit rather than by inspection. The check is finer than nonemptiness of the class: every Peirce rule mentioning the half-eigenspace would be vacuously true on a carrier where that space is trivial, and it is trivial for the two idempotents one reaches for first, so a witness with nonzero half-eigenspace is exhibited on H_2(C).
Every declaration in the tracked tree has an axiom closure contained in Lean's three core axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The tree carries no custom axiom, no sorry and no native_decide.

records.title: catskillsresearch/scott1980
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / mathlib formalization of Dana Scott's 1980 Oxford lectures, published May 1981 as PRG-19 Lectures on a Mathematical Theory of Computation. The principal sourced Palomar result is the first sentence of Theorem 8.8: the neighbourhood system U over [0,1) ⊆ ℚ is universal, in the sense that every countable neighbourhood system D embeds as a subdomain (D ⊴ U). Comparator also selects two new formal corollaries: P4_embeds for Scott's Example 1.5 and Ssys_embeds for Exercise 7.22. Scott defines those systems but does not separately state the embeddings. Challenge.lean fixes the neighbourhood-system vocabulary, including Scott's standing assumption that the master token set Δ is non-empty, Scott's ⊴, and the concrete Definition 8.7 family U. This foundational universality result supplies a concrete host for all countable domains; it is relevant to domain theory, denotational semantics, mathematical logic, and formalized mathematics. The broader Lectures I–VIII development lives in Scott1980/Neighborhood/* and is not the advertised Comparator result. The informal account is arxiv.md; the working transcription is sources/PRG19.md. Lean was written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. Dana Scott did not participate in or endorse this formalization. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.

records.title: rwst/Confinement-Certificates
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper on the emptiness theory of the sets Z_{p/q}(s, s+t) = {ξ > 0 : {ξ(p/q)ⁿ} ∈ [s, s+t) for all n ≥ 0}, the generalized Z-numbers of Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington, at and beyond the window length 1/p. The paper introduces block certificates --- finite integer witnesses, rechecked from scratch by the Lean proof kernel, whose soundness rests on the aperiodicity lemma alone --- and uses them to pass the length-$1/p$ line: $\Zset_{3/2}(1/6,13/24)=\emptyset$ (window length $3/8>1/3$), $\Zset_{3/2}(961/3600,2427/3600)=\emptyset$ (length $733/1800$), and explicit unions of total length up to $17/24$, against $20/39$ in print. The closed-interval union statement of Dubickas is replicated exactly as printed; no $\xi\ne0$ keeps $\|\xi(3/2)^{n}\|<1/5$ for every $n$, with $\|\cdot\|$ the distance to the nearest integer; and thirty windows of length $1/p$ are certified at five bases in the regime $p>q^{2}$ that Dubickas leaves open. There is no sorry anywhere outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and no native_decide: every block certificate is discharged by `c.ok = true := by decide`, i.e. by kernel reduction of integer arithmetic on the certificate's raw data.

records.title: catskillsresearch/scott1972
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / mathlib formalization of Dana Scott's 1972 paper *Continuous Lattices* (LNM 274), through the Milner correction (pp. 135–136). The Palomar compared result is Theorem 4.4 as worded in sources/ScottContinLatt1972.md: the inverse limit D_∞ of the recursively defined sequence ⟨D_n, j_n⟩ of function spaces is not only a continuous lattice, but it is also homeomorphic to its own function space [D_∞ → D_∞]. The compared Homeomorph explicitly uses the product/subspace topology on the inverse limit and the pointwise Pi topology on the function space. The full paper development (injectivity, Scott topology, way-below, function spaces, inverse limits) lives in Scott1972/ContinuousLattice/*. The informal account is arxiv.md and sources/ScottContinLatt1972.md in this repository. Lean was written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. Dana Scott did not participate in or endorse this formalization. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.

records.title: jeremypparker/mahler-hansen-cograph
records.abstract: A Lean 4/Mathlib formalisation of a sharp Mahler-volume theorem for Hansen polytopes of finite cographs. It proves that the normalized Mahler volume of the Hansen polytope of a cograph is at least one, and exactly one if and only if it is a threshold graph.

records.title: catskillsresearch/scott1982
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / mathlib formalization of Dana Scott's 1982 ICALP paper *Domains for Denotational Semantics*. The Palomar compared result is only the first sentence of Theorem 7.2: if A and B are information systems, then so is A → B, and the approximable mappings f : A → B are exactly the elements f ∈ |A → B|. Challenge.lean imports Mathlib only and locks Definition 2.1, Definition 2.2, Definition 5.1, and Definition 7.1 (tokens, consistency, and the constructive-witness form of entailment). The remaining apply / curry clauses of the same numbered theorem live in Scott1982/Theorem72.lean and are not Comparator targets. The informal account is arxiv.md; ground truth for theorem wording is sources/Domains_for_Denotational_Semantics.pdf. Lean was written by AI agents under the direction and review of the author. Dana Scott did not participate in or endorse this formalization. There is no sorry outside the deliberate holes in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.

records.title: xiangyazi24/palomar-qseries-row-factorization
records.abstract: A Lean 4 verification of an explicit rank-two indefinite theta completion over Q(sqrt(5)). The registered results cover the coefficientwise row-model factorization; the exact holomorphic-sign-part bridge; summability of the defining completed-theta lattice series; a specialization of Zwegers' Lemma 2.8; the weight-one T and S transformations, including the five-to-two characteristic reduction; the exact mixed boundary derivative and Bruinier--Funke image; and a kernel-checked nonharmonicity witness.

records.title: balancedscorpion/shifted-square-root-fourier-classification
records.abstract: For 0 < θ < 1, this Lean 4 formalization classifies tempered atomic measures whose support and Fourier support are contained in the shifted square-root set Λθ = {±√(n + θ) | n ∈ ℕ₀}. In an equivalent polynomial-growth coefficient model, it proves that the −1 and i Fourier eigenspaces vanish, identifies the surviving 1 and −i eigenspaces as one-dimensional lines generated by explicit generalized eta products up to the respective thresholds θ ≤ 1/8 and θ ≤ 3/8, and proves that the full admissible space has dimension 2, 1, or 0 in the resulting three θ ranges.

records.title: dcposch/jc2-lean
records.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of a two-sheet implication in the aligned nontrivial cubic-Kummer analysis at actual partial degrees (6,9). Every field-valued solution of the four lower-Pfaffian invariant equations is proved to lie on a common-power sheet with zero source bracket or on an elliptic sheet; converse inclusions and existence of the sheets are not compared.  The formalization derives the elliptic equation and terminal one-form, excludes nonconstant reduced rational trajectories on its C != 0 fibre by a finite forbidden-value argument, factors the C=0 fibre, and verifies the shifted Davenport--Stothers bracket and terminal descent. Version 2 derives the finite-place valuation classification directly from the reduced rational ODE, proves the one-point support theorem, and excludes that sheet in the noncube Kummer branch.  It does not claim the preceding landing from an arbitrary Keller pair, the cube branch, all (6,9), maximum eleven, or JC2.

records.title: catskillsresearch/scott_models
records.abstract: Order isomorphisms relating Scott’s three presentations of domains — continuous lattices (1972), neighbourhood systems (PRG-19), and information systems (1982) — including the round identification D ≃o RoundFilter ≃o RoundInfoSysElement and the S-expression equation T ≅ A + (T × T) as |T| ≃o |A + (T × T)| (SexSys.Element ≃o SexRhs.Element). records.title: teal-sea/zeta-lab
records.abstract: Let N(T,2T) count the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with ordinate in (T,2T], with multiplicity, and N_0^s(T,2T) the simple zeros among them on the critical line. The Lean development accompanying arXiv:2608.13637 (anthropics/zeta-23-lean) proves, for Mathlib's riemannZeta and unconditionally, that for every eps > 0 and all large T, (H - eps) N(T,2T) <= N_0^s(T,2T), with H = 3/2 - (1/sqrt 2) cot(1/sqrt 2) = 0.67250070367941164573... (its Theorem D). Ainta (github.com/ainta/zeta-simple-zeros) refines H by carrying the spectral defect of the Gram matrix of the simple-zero vectors through that argument and bounding it block by block through a local inequality on seven points. Advertised here: that refinement carried out for n points at once, and three instances. Parametrically, for n >= 2, c > 0, m >= n, p > 0 with c(m-(n-1)) <= 1, if c <= F(n,p,g) for every nonnegative vector g of n-1 gaps (the hypothesis hCert), then for every eps > 0 and all large T, (Phi_n(n,c,m,p) - eps) N(T,2T) <= N_0^s(T,2T), where Phi_n(n,c,m,p) = (H - (n-1)(m-1)/(pm)) / (1 - c(m-(n-1))/m). At n = 7 this is Ainta's theorem. THE THREE-POINT INSTANCE IS UNCONDITIONAL. At (n,c,p) = (3, 1345/10^6, 3000) the hypothesis is proved, not assumed: the overlap weight w = k^2 is enclosed from a twelve-term Taylor bound on cos and sin and the closed form of the kernel, and 368 interval cell lemmas over rationals, applied 1515 times over 487 leaves, cover the quarter-plane of the two gaps. No external interval-arithmetic certificate is assumed for the three-point theorem, and no floating point appears. The cap gives m = 745 and the constant (149000000 H - 99200)/148800133 = 0.67273733450380945875..., exceeding H by 2.3663e-4: for Mathlib's riemannZeta, an unconditional improvement of the dependency's Theorem D. THE FOUR-POINT INSTANCE IS ALSO UNCONDITIONAL. At (n,c,p) = (4, 2310/10^6, 2500), the finite inequality at every triple of nonnegative gaps is proved inside Lean. The cap gives m = 435 and the resulting constant is (906250 H - 1085)/904171 = 0.67284701976668870316.... The bound and ratio carry no certificate hypothesis and use exactly the same three permitted axioms. The eight-point instance stays conditional. Our n-point generalisation of Ainta's interval verifier accepts c = 41763/10^7 at p = 3200, giving m = 246 and 0.67305298298962888...; interval-arithmetic acceptance is not a Lean proof, so hCert remains explicit. The contrast is explicit in the statements: the parametric and eight-point theorems retain a named certificate hypothesis, while the three- and four-point theorems prove their certificates inside Lean.

records.title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
records.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Graham–Pollak theorem (1971) and its tightness on complete bipartite partitions of complete graphs. Proves that any partition of the edges of the complete graph K_n into m complete bipartite subgraphs requires at least n - 1 bipartite graphs (m >= n - 1), adapting Helge Tverberg's 1982 linear-algebraic quadratic form argument. Also formalizes the canonical star partition proving tightness. To the maintainers' knowledge, Graham–Pollak was not previously formalized in Mathlib (checked against Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: lukasliehr/GrothendieckBessel
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the existence assertion in Theorem 1.1 of arXiv:2608.12280v1 with the sharp constant K = 1: for every countable Bessel sequence with bound 1 in a complex Hilbert space, there exist measurable functions on the unit interval, pointwise bounded by 1, whose correlations reproduce the sequence's Gram matrix. This solves an open problem posed by Olevskii.

records.title: JaTaSn/lattice-line-covers
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.22550: there is a family of lattice lines covering the integer plane whose set of realized directions is dense. Concretely, a family F of subsets of Z^2 is exhibited such that (i) every member is a genuine lattice line, the nonempty solution set of Px + Qy = c with P, Q coprime; (ii) the members cover Z^2; (iii) two members of different direction are disjoint, so no lattice point is covered twice in different directions; and (iv) the directions that occur are dense in the space RP^1 of line directions, that is, every angle in [0, pi) is approximated to within any epsilon by the direction of some member. The construction is recursive and works on nested regions: a chain of cosets Z^2 = R_0 > R_1 > R_2 > ... is built, and at stage k the region R_k is partitioned into sub-cosets of a new coprime direction, one of which is reserved to become R_{k+1} while lines of that direction claim all the others. Coverage is what the choice of reserved sub-coset is for: fix a surjective enumeration z_0, z_1, ... of Z^2 and reserve, at stage k, a sub-coset that does not contain z_k -- always possible, since the partition has at least four sub-cosets and only the one containing z_k must be avoided. Every point is then claimed: it is z_k for some k, and either it had already left the region at an earlier stage, in which case the coverage invariant Z^2 \ R_k = union over i < k of (R_i \ R_{i+1}) shows it was claimed there, or it is still in R_k and the reservation rule places it in a sub-coset claimed at stage k. Reserving an arbitrary sub-coset would not do: without that diagonal choice a point could survive in every R_k and never be claimed. Disjointness is a consequence of that partition rather than of any criterion for when two individual lines meet: distinct sub-cosets of a region are disjoint, each stage's lines stay inside the sub-cosets they claim, and the regions claimed at distinct stages are therefore disjoint. Earlier lines survive untouched because everything a later stage touches lies inside the reserved region. Only Theorem 1 is formalized; the paper's further remarks and discussion are not.

records.title: JD-Jones-ASES/fs-formal
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of an explicit construction for the Furstenberg-Sárközy problem. If D(N) is the largest size of a subset of {1,...,N} with no nonzero square difference, the development proves that an explicit eleven-block constant alphaInf is at most liminf log D(N)/log N, that every exponent below alphaInf holds eventually pointwise, and that 0.7537 < alphaInf. The proof includes the finite certificates, the composite even-digit lift, CRT gluing, asymptotic passage, and kernel-checked numerical inequalities. This strictly improves Krachun's preceding explicit exponent 0.752796455874514... and moves the lower bound farther beyond 3/4.

records.title: Polylogarithmic Descent for Almost All Collatz Orbits in Natural Density
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of four strengthened almost-all results for shortcut and raw Collatz orbits in ordinary natural density: critical polylogarithmic descent with arbitrary positive divergent target and height multipliers, centered trajectory tubes, and actual first-passage clocks; the fixed-exponent common-landing theorem with the exact upper exceptional-rate endpoint; an explicit reciprocal-order lower bound forced by the joint height ceiling; and a quantitative stretched-logarithmic common-landing theorem with smaller relative-height ceilings. These are almost-all statements and do not prove pointwise Collatz convergence.

records.title: g-pichler/bsc-averaging
records.abstract:
A Lean 4 / Mathlib development that settles three previously open problems about
binary channels on a doubly symmetric binary source (DSBS): a pair (X, Y) of Bernoulli(1/2)
bits with P(X != Y) = p, together with Markov chains U - X - Y - V in which U and V are the
outputs of two independent binary channels applied to X and to Y. All quantities are in nats.

(1) MathOverflow 285151, "Do averaged binary symmetric channels maximize mutual information?"
(Georg Pichler, 2017; unanswered there) asks whether conv A = conv B, where A is the set of
rate triples (R0, R1, R2) with I(U;X) <= R1, I(Y;V) <= R2 and R0 <= I(U;V) attainable by
arbitrary binary channels on the two sides, and B is the same set with both channels
restricted to be binary symmetric. The inclusion B subset A is elementary; the question is
whether taking convex hulls closes the gap, which the counterexample to the predecessor
question MathOverflow 213084 leaves open. This development proves conv A = conv B for every
p in [0,1] (`averaged_bsc_maximise_mutual_information`). The same statement settles
Conjecture 5.2 of Pichler, Piantanida and Matz, "Distributed Information-Theoretic
Clustering", Information and Inference 11 (2022) 1029-1082.

(2), (3) Conjectures 1 and 2 of Dikshtein, Ordentlich and Shamai (Shitz), "The Double-Sided
Information Bottleneck Function", Entropy 24(9):1321 (2022), which concern the double-sided
information bottleneck function R(Cu, Cv) = max I(U;V) subject to I(X;U) <= Cu and
I(Y;V) <= Cv at p = 0, that is X = Y. Conjecture 1 predicts that the maximising test channels
are a Z-channel and an S-channel; Conjecture 2 predicts that the pair maximising I(X;U,V) are
both Z-channels. Both are proved here for binary U and V, in optimality form: the Challenge
statements exhibit the conjectured channels themselves as `Chan` values and say that no
admissible pair beats them. No admissible pair exceeds the I(U;V) of the Z/S pair
(`conjecture1_p0_holds`), and none undercuts that of the Z/Z pair (`conjecture2_p0_holds`), at
every nondegenerate rate pair. A Z-channel and an S-channel are the same transition matrix up
