The compositum half, for the degree-12 minimal polynomial of rho * Q (written out in full in every compared statement): (5) an exclusion witness — a nonreal quartic root z with 1 < |rho * z| < rho * Q; (6) the twelve embedding products ARE the conjugates of rho * Q, both directions; (7) there are exactly twelve of them; (8) rho * Q is an algebraic unit, via an explicit degree-11 cofactor over any commutative ring — the (3, 4, 12) triple in the normal form alpha * beta * gamma = 1; (9) the degree-12 polynomial is not reciprocal (neither its reversal nor the reversal's negation), placing it in the regime of Smyth's theorem; (10) degree multiplicativity — deg minpoly(rho*Q) = deg minpoly(rho) * deg minpoly(Q) = 12; (11) the compositum in sup form Q(rho) join Q(Q) = Q(rho*Q), of degree 12, with the two simple extensions linearly disjoint; (12) the complete unit-circle census — EXACTLY 5 conjugates strictly outside, EXACTLY 7 strictly inside, NONE on the circle, so rho * Q is neither a Pisot nor a Salem number; (13) the house — every conjugate other than rho * Q has modulus strictly below rho * Q; (14) the exact Mahler measure M = rho^2 * Q^2 * psi, where psi is the real root > 1 of psi^4 = psi^3 + 1; (15) the registry bridge — M(X^4 - X - 1) = psi and M(rulerPoly) = (rho * Q)^2 * M(X^4 - X - 1), re-proving in-repo the quantity pinned in registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004; (16) the order-12 Hadamard product recurrence — the termwise product of any solutions of the cubic and quartic shift recurrences satisfies the order-12 recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is exactly the degree-12 polynomial, in any Q-algebra; (17) the annihilator ideal of the product power sequence n |-> (rho * Q)^n is EXACTLY the principal ideal of the degree-12 polynomial — the classical order <= 3 * 4 bound is an equality, forced by the polynomial's kernel-held irreducibility. The results address three research audiences: the degree problem for products and composita of algebraic numbers (the certified (3,4,12) witness at a canonically distinguished pair, in the field's own unit-product normal form); the Mahler-measure tradition (the measure of the composed product of the two degree-minimal polynomials, in closed form in the second-smallest Pisot number); and composed products of polynomials (a certified rational instance where the finite-field coprimality criterion is unavailable and irreducibility is proved by elimination) — with the Lean audience served by concrete exercise of the Mahler-measure and linear-disjointness APIs. Like the golden ratio, rho * Q is an algebraic unit of norm -1; the compared cofactor identity is that norm computation, certified. No novelty claim is made for the measure identity (the entry is not aware of it in the literature; the claimed contribution is the kernel certificate), no "first formalization" claim is made anywhere, and whether rho is ATTAINED as a dynamical degree is open in the literature — no statement claims it. Hypotheses are inline: rho, Q, psi enter only through their defining equations plus root-selection inequalities, and the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (Filter.Tendsto, nhds, the complex norm, minpoly, Polynomial.rootSet, Set.ncard, Polynomial.mahlerMeasure, IntermediateField adjoin/sup, Module.finrank, Finset.range sums) — zero custom definitions. The name prefix "ruler" in statement names is the source project's term for the product rho * Q; nothing in any statement depends on it.

records.title: hadamard-b-formal: the bordered Goethals-Seidel characterisation, the s=1 layer, and Theorem D
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of part of the theorem layer of the Hadamard-B note on bordered Goethals-Seidel arrays: twenty-six compared theorems over fifty-eight compared definitions. Theorem A characterises, by an if-and-only-if, when a Goethals-Seidel array of four sign-valued sequences over a finite abelian group extends to a Hadamard matrix through a border of width 4s whose strips are constant on the cosets of a subgroup. Theorem B is its house form, whose hypothesis is exactly a two-tier periodic-autocorrelation profile, and carries two classical degenerations at an arbitrary reflection shift: the Goethals-Seidel theorem over an arbitrary finite abelian group, and the Wallis-Whiteman/Spence bordered construction. Of Theorem C only the row-sum rows D5 and D6 are formalized; clauses D1-D4 and the classification corollary are not. The character-twist layer is Lemma T, the s = 1 profile bijection, and the theorem that a twist fixing the reflection shift is a diagonal conjugation. Theorem D is covered at clauses (D-a) through (D-e): the forced Gram and border tables, the collapse of (H4) to a single 4x4 equation, the integer Parseval identity, both directions of the transport across the doubling, and clause (D-a'), which identifies the degenerate branch with the index-one construction entry for entry, again in both directions. The index-two collapse corollary is represented by its seed-problem bijection clause alone; its characteristic-subgroup and equivariance clauses are not formalized, nor is the 768-squared census behind (D-e). Two witness records are imported under SHA-256 pins, cross-checked against the source's canonical matrix digests, and checked by kernel reduction against Theorem A's hypotheses, giving Hadamard matrices of orders 52 and 20 through the theorem rather than by matrix multiplication; no novelty of existence is claimed at either order.

records.title: Native Lean equality-saturation certificate checking
records.abstract: Formalizes a native Lean checker for certified finite acyclic e-graphs. The principal result proves that accepted class certificates connect a canonical e-class term to the executable extracted representative and establish its minimum additive cost among all represented terms. The development also covers chronological merge certificates, egg-style flat explanations, replay-backed extraction, and bounded certificate search.

records.title: Only two morphic numbers: the Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer classification of the golden ratio and the plastic number
records.abstract: Kernel-checked classification of the morphic numbers — the reals p > 1 satisfying both of the golden ratio's defining scale closures: p + 1 = p^k (the sum of consecutive measures of the geometric system is again a measure) and p - 1 = p^(-l) (so is their difference; rendered zpow-free as p^l * (p - 1) = 1). These two equations are the arithmetic of self-similar proportion: a number satisfying both generates a measure system closed under the paper's superposition and juxtaposition, the property pair behind the divine proportion's standing as the plane's design constant. The theorem (Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer 2001): there exist only two such numbers — the golden ratio, with (k, l) = (2, 1), and the plastic number, the real root of x^3 = x + 1, with (k, l) = (3, 4). Four compared statements carry the classification in full: existence of the cubic's root, the iff pinning every morphic number to the golden ratio or that root, and the two witnesses. The list of numbers with the golden ratio's defining property pair is thereby provably complete at two. The second member is a distinguished constant independently of this theorem: the plastic number is the smallest Pisot number (Siegel 1944); its minimal polynomial x^3 - x - 1 attains the minimal Mahler measure among monic irreducible integer cubics (kernel-certified in the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004), and by Smyth's theorem its measure — the number itself — is the global minimum of the Mahler measure over nonreciprocal integer polynomials; it is the growth rate of the Padovan and Perrin sequences, the cubic analogue of Fibonacci growth; and it is the threshold constant of the Blanc-Cantat classification of birational surface dynamical degrees, the spectral limit of the Bedford-Kim automorphism family (kernel-certified in the author's mahler-minimizer-compositum entry). It entered mathematics from architecture: Dom Hans van der Laan introduced it (Le Nombre Plastique, 1960) as the ideal ratio of three-dimensional proportion — the same discovery made independently by Cordonnier — and Kruijtzer conjectured, and Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer proved, that van der Laan's number is the only companion the golden ratio has. What "morphic" adds to the plastic number's distinctions is finality: the golden ratio's arithmetic of self-similarity, taken as a definition, has exactly one more solution among the reals. The formalized proof consumes Selmer's trinomial irreducibility theorem from Mathlib, derives the needed Tverberg-type instance through a mirror-dichotomy argument carried out entirely in the integer polynomial ring (simplifying the paper's complex-root analysis; disclosed in the fidelity block), and closes with the factorization endgame forcing (n, m) = (3, 5). No formalization of the morphic classification, the plastic number, or the Padovan/Perrin constants exists in any surveyed prover as of the 2026-09-01 sweep; Mathlib's golden-ratio development supplies one witness's vocabulary. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

records.title: Howson's theorem through finite cores and Kurosh decomposition
records.abstract: Formalizes Howson's theorem for finite-rank free groups: the intersection of two finitely generated subgroups is finitely generated. The proof uses the repository's inclusion-compatible Marshall Hall construction to place one subgroup as a free factor of a finite-index overgroup, applies Schreier's finite-index theorem to the other subgroup, and then uses the actual Kurosh decomposition of the resulting subgroup of a binary free product. The final map from the relevant conjugate-intersection factor is defined from the factor inclusions and proved surjective onto the internal subgroup intersection.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: Proof-Carrying Decreasing-Diagram Confluence Certificates
records.abstract: A Lean 4.33.0 formalization of a generic soundness theorem for finite, proof-carrying decreasing-diagram certificates. An artifact lists the labeled rewrite steps and explicit decreasing valleys for every local peak; an executable checker validates the finite data, while a separate completeness proof connects that data to the semantic relation. The theorem assumes `WellFounded lt` for the label order and then derives confluence of the unlabeled relation even though the underlying rewrite relation itself need not terminate. The repository includes a nontrivial funnel regression with three local peaks and negative certificate tests, plus a generated family study of canonical compression.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: Arrow's theorem via Fourier analysis
records.abstract: This is a formalization in Lean 4 of Arrow's theorem for three-candidate elections as stated in Ryan O'Donnell's book "Analysis of Boolean Functions", Sec. 2.5, with a single voting rule applied to every pairwise election. The theorem states that every unanimous voting rule that always admits a Condorcet winner  must be a dictatorship, i.e. there must exist a voter that alone determines the outcome. Here voting rules are encoded by Boolean-valued functions on the Hamming cube. The proof follows the exposition given there, which is based on Gil Kalai's Fourier-analytic argument using the Walsh-Fourier transform. The version stated in the book  and formalized here is not the most general version of Arrow's theorem: for example, one may allow more than three candidates, or that the voting rules for each pairwise election are different. This formalization was entirely human-written.

records.title: The golden family's boundary at n = 3: general-n theorems for x^n = x + 1
records.abstract: Kernel-checked general-n theorems for the golden family — the ladder of trinomials x^n - x - 1, whose unique real root r_n > 1 descends from the golden ratio (n = 2) through the plastic number (n = 3) toward 1. The family's structural boundary falls at n = 3; this entry proves the morphic half unconditionally at general n and holds the Pisot half as the measure⟺Pisot equivalence, the unconditional n = 4 non-Pisot statement, and the Siegel-conditional strict excess for n >= 4, from the family's own arithmetic, with no per-degree case check above the boundary. Eleven compared statements carry the surface. (1) The root ladder: for every n >= 2 the root exists, is unique above 1, and strictly decreases in n. (2) The morphic boundary, UNCONDITIONAL: r_n satisfies the golden ratio's two scale closures p + 1 = p^k and p - 1 = p^(-l) (Aarts-Fokkink-Kruijtzer 2001, spelled inline) if and only if n <= 3 — the classification pins morphic numbers to the golden ratio and the plastic number, and descent puts r_n below 1.23, hence below both, for n >= 4. (3) Circle exclusion: x^n - x - 1 has no complex root of modulus 1, for any n (|z| = |z + 1| = 1 forces z^2 + z + 1 = 0, so z^3 = 1, and every residue of n mod 3 is impossible). (4) The Jensen lower bound r_n <= M(x^n - x - 1), by the monic root-product form of the Mahler measure. (5) The equivalence M(x^n - x - 1) = r_n iff every other complex root lies strictly inside the unit circle — the honest form of "the family's Mahler-measure boundary IS its Pisot boundary": the equivalence is itself the kernel theorem (exact because the family never has unimodular roots, and its trinomials are separable by Selmer irreducibility), stated once and never counted as a pair of separate boundaries. (6) The Siegel-conditional closure: IF the plastic number is the smallest Pisot number — Siegel 1944, entering ONLY as an explicit named hypothesis, with "Pisot" unfolded in the statement — THEN r_n < M(x^n - x - 1) for every n >= 4. Siegel's minimality is the single classical input anywhere in the entry; every other statement is kernel-checked unconditionally, and Siegel's theorem itself is not proved here. (7) Q < psi: the quartic root (q^4 = q + 1) lies strictly below psi (psi^4 = psi^3 + 1), the Mahler measure of the n = 4 member. (8) THE SHARED LEMMA, at general n: no root of x^n - x - 1 satisfies z^2 + z + 1 = 0 (z^3 = 1 and every residue of n mod 3 is impossible). It supplies the obstruction in the circle exclusion (3), which is re-derived from it as an explicit corollary (the circle geometry supplies the reduction), and up to the substitution z^n = z + 1 (under which z^n + z^2 = 0 iff z^2 + z + 1 = 0) it is Mathlib's public Polynomial.X_pow_sub_X_sub_one_irreducible_aux — the first step of Mathlib's Selmer proof, hence of the morphic classification behind (2) — restated in the family's own vocabulary; compared as the named shared core, not as new mathematics. (9) Witness b_3 (b^3 = b^2 + 1): every other complex root of x^3 = x^2 + 1 has modulus < 1, and b_3 is not morphic. (10) Witness psi (psi^4 = psi^3 + 1): every other complex root of x^4 = x^3 + 1 has modulus < 1, and psi is not morphic. (11) The golden quartic root is NOT Pisot: for q^4 = q + 1, some complex root of x^4 = x + 1 other than q has modulus > 1 (every nonreal root does — quartic_conj_norm_gt_one in the proof module, not compared) — with (10) and (7) the degree-4 separation: Q and psi are both algebraic units with constant term of modulus one (unit-ness is elementary and not compared: Q^-1 = Q^3 - 1, psi^-1 = psi^3 - psi^2), yet Q is not Pisot and psi is, so the unit condition alone does not locate the Pisot boundary. (10) and (11) are not independent evidence: x^4 - x^3 - 1 is the image of x^4 - x - 1 under x -> -1/x, so the Pisot half of (10) says x^4 - x - 1 has one root inside the unit circle and three outside, and (11) follows; they are compared separately for the two families' sakes. THE STORY: one shared lemma beneath both boundaries (naming the family-specific arithmetic core, not the whole proof graph: (2) and (6) also share the elementary descent r_n < 1.23 < rho, and the kernel-held Pisot side is localized by Siegel plus descent, the angle route being context); the boundaries localize by different routes — an angle for Pisot (the escape arc between the primitive cube roots of unity, giving the outside-root count 1 + 2*floor((2n - 1)/6), Howell-Kyle 2018 Theorem 3 via the reciprocal trinomial; context, NOT formalized), a degree for morphic (the cofactor x^2 - x + 1 forcing k = 3; formalized) — and the classes are in fact separable: (9)-(11) hold the witnesses and the degree-4 separation in the kernel, with no Siegel input, showing the classes coming apart inside the sister trinomial family itself (Pisot units below phi that are not morphic). The entry never claims the two boundaries are independent (they share the lemma) and never claims a common cause for their location. Two spellings of "Pisot" appear: the trinomial-roots form of (5), (9), (10), (11) and the minimal-polynomial form of the siegel hypothesis; they coincide exactly when the defining trinomial is irreducible (Selmer for (5), (11); x^3 - x^2 - 1 and x^4 - x^3 - 1 have no rational root and no integer quadratic factorization, for (9), (10)). On the sister family x^m - x^(m-1) - 1 the classes come apart: b_2 = phi and b_5 = rho exactly, so morphic only for m = 2, 5 (AFK, kernel-held, plus strict decrease); Pisot at m = 2, 5 is elementary, though at m = 5 the quintic is reducible with two roots ON the unit circle, so b_5 is Pisot in the minimal-polynomial sense only; the m = 3, 4 members are the kernel-held witnesses; not Pisot for 6 <= m <= 30 numerically and for all m >= 6 Siegel-conditionally (b_6 < rho). The n <= 4 instances of this boundary are registered content of the author's sibling entries (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004, PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005, and PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000008) and are cited as context imports, never re-compared. The classical route to the n >= 4 strict excess (Smyth 1971), the limit behavior of the family measures (Lawton 1983, Smyth 1981, Verger-Gaugry 2016, Stankov 2014), and the outside-root count (Howell-Kyle 2018, with Brilleslyper-Schaubroeck 2014 for the unimodular criterion and Stankov 2014 for the asymptotic density) are cited context, not formalized — see the labeled context block in the sources. As of the 2026-09-01 sweep the entry is not aware of a prior formalization of the general-n family boundary, of Siegel minimality, of Smyth's nonreciprocal bound, or of Pisot-number theory in any surveyed prover ecosystem; Mathlib supplies Selmer irreducibility and the Mahler-measure development as infrastructure. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

records.title: Grushko--Neumann rank additivity for free products
records.abstract: Formalizes the binary Grushko--Neumann theorem: the minimal number of generators of a free product of two finitely generated groups is the sum of the minimal numbers of generators of the factors. The central theorem is proved by a kernel-checked finite labelled-graph reduction. For a minimal null path, the implemented reduction uniformly performs a source unfold, a subsequent safe fold, and an explicit monochromatic-vertex contraction; this gives the strict decrease used by strong induction and the separated-generator lower bound. The repository also retains the finite-core and free-group rank lemmas from the surrounding development as reusable supporting infrastructure, but only the global Grushko theorem declaration is selected by the public Challenge and Comparator.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: Generalized Markoff strong approximation
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the generic branch of eventual strong approximation for generalized Markoff surfaces, specialized to a fixed ordered integral coefficient triple. It proves punctured transitivity for both the full Vieta group and the two-Vieta rotation group, supplies an explicit coefficient-dependent cutoff, and derives surjectivity of coordinatewise reduction onto the full finite-field surface.

records.title: Actual F₂ flag homology and the dense extremal counterexample family
records.abstract: A finite-chain formalization of the F₂ content of Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 3.1 in the source paper. Lean defines the literal flag-chain groups of a finite graph using unordered edges and three-vertex clique faces, their d1 and d2 maps, and actual H1 as ker(d1)/range(d2). It proves that the paper's family G_n has F₂ first Betti number exactly two for every n at least seven, proves the universal F₂ upper bound beta1 <= 2 for every n-vertex graph with choose(n,2)-n edges, and bundles these facts with the exact density and no-complete-bipartite-spanning obstruction. The literal d1-d2 identity is also selected so every Challenge proof hole is compared. No compared proof uses native_decide or an external homology axiom.

records.title: Salem's theorem: every Pisot number is a two-sided limit of Salem numbers
records.abstract: Kernel-checked Salem's theorem — every Pisot number is a limit point of Salem numbers from both sides (R. Salem, Algebraic Numbers and Fourier Analysis, D. C. Heath, 1963, Ch. III, Theorem IV, p. 30; origin R. Salem, Duke Math. J. 12 (1945)) — with both of Salem's constructions, each stated as a construction. Three compared statements carry the surface. (1) salem_theorem — the theorem for Pisot numbers: a real algebraic integer alpha > 1 every other complex root of whose minimal polynomial has modulus < 1 (spelled as 1 < alpha, IsIntegral Z alpha, and every z in (minpoly Q alpha).aroots C other than alpha has norm < 1 — the spelling of the Pisot predicate in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, inlined) has, for every eps > 0, a Salem number in (alpha - eps, alpha) and one in (alpha, alpha + eps). (2) salem_construction_two_sided — Salem's main construction z^m P(z) ± z^p P(1/z) with its family root in the conclusion: for the pattern data of a monic integer polynomial P (one real root alpha > 1, every other complex root strictly inside the unit circle, conjugation-closed) under the nondegeneracy P(1/alpha) != 0 — a proviso that on the pattern domain is strictly STRONGER than Boyd's — coinciding, when P is the minimal polynomial, with Boyd's "provided P is not a reciprocal quadratic" (Math. Comp. 32 (1978), p. 1252, eq. (26)) and with the reason clause of Salem's, "so that Q and P will not be identical" (Salem's stated hypothesis, "theta not a quadratic unit", is stronger; fidelity (g)) — there is a sign e = ±1, the sign of P(1/alpha), such that for every eps > 0 some X^m P + e P.reverse with m >= 2 has a Salem root in (alpha - eps, alpha) and some X^m P - e P.reverse with m >= 2 has a Salem root in (alpha, alpha + eps); P.reverse is z^p P(1/z), p = deg P. (3) salem_quadratic_unit — the excluded case, Salem's second construction (1963, p. 31) with its family root in the conclusion: for the reciprocal quadratic Pisot units alpha^2 = r alpha - 1, r >= 3 an integer, and every eps > 0, some (X^2 - rX + 1)(X^{2m} + 1) + X^{m+1} with m >= 1 has a Salem root in (alpha - eps, alpha) and some (X^2 - rX + 1)(X^{2m} + 1) - X^{m+1} with m >= 1 has a Salem root in (alpha, alpha + eps) — the Chebyshev family (x - r) T_m(x) ∓ 1 pulled back through x = y + 1/y. Statement (1) is the theorem; (2) and (3) each carry their construction and neither follows from (1), their conclusions naming a root of a specific polynomial; Boyd's "for all sufficiently large m" is NOT stated — (2) and (3) assert, per eps, the existence of some index m. A Salem number is spelled by Salem's definition of the class T (1963, p. 26): a real algebraic integer tau > 1 all of whose other conjugates lie in the closed unit disk, at least one on the unit circle — with the clause that 1/tau is a conjugate stated explicitly. Classically that clause and "degree at least 4" are consequences (Salem 1963, p. 26; Smyth 2015, Lemma 1); the equivalence is NOT formalized here, and the formal predicate is the stronger conjunction, which is the CONCLUSION of every compared statement — nothing is assumed of it. THE ROUTE: (1) is transported from a pattern-form theorem in the proof modules (salem_theorem_full), stated for any monic integer polynomial with the pattern data — a larger index set than the Pisot numbers (X^k times a minimal polynomial has the pattern) but equivalent in content, since the large root of any pattern polynomial is itself a Pisot number — through the bridge that the minimal polynomial over Z of a Pisot number carries the pattern data (the Gauss step: the minimal polynomial over Q is the rational image of the one over Z, since Z is integrally closed; separability of the irreducible minimal polynomial in characteristic zero; conjugation-invariance of integer coefficients). The pattern-form theorem splits on P(1/alpha) = 0: the nonzero branch is the assembly PdtSalemEndgame.salem_two_sided; the zero branch reduces to PdtSalemQuadUnit.salem_two_sided_quad_unit by a supporting lemma (reciprocal_quadratic_of_inv_root: a pattern polynomial vanishing at 1/alpha forces alpha^2 = r alpha - 1 with r >= 3 — the elementary "reciprocal Pisot implies quadratic", McKee–Smyth 2012, Lemma 6.2). Those two assemblies discard the index and the family; (2) and (3) are the same assemblies re-run in the bridge module SalemPisot with both kept. The book runs Case 1 under the proviso and handles the quadratic units in Case 2; the kernel unifies both cases in a single statement with no nondegeneracy hypothesis — a presentational unification of Salem's own two cases, not a mathematical strengthening of the theorem, which has no gap. The proofs use no argument principle and no Rouché theorem: the circle counts (m + p - 2 unimodular roots for the plus family z^m P + z^p P(1/z) with p = deg P, m + p - 3 plus the root z = 1 for the minus family, 2m for the quadratic-unit family) are intermediate-value arguments on explicit real phases; the trichotomy (every root unimodular or in {tau, 1/tau}) is a multiset squeeze against the degree; Salem-ness is an arithmetic certificate (the minimal polynomial divides the family; the Gauss step excludes degrees 1 and 2 and forces 1/tau a conjugate), with the integer degeneracies tau in Z and tau + 1/tau in Z discharged by finiteness along the ladders, or directly for the quadratic-unit family. NOT formalized: the equivalence of the Salem-number definitions (above); Boyd's converse (Boyd 1977: every Salem number arises from the construction); Salem 1944 (the Pisot numbers form a closed set); any rate of approach; Boyd's "for all sufficiently large m". As of the 2026-09-01 sweep (Mathlib at the pin and at master, Loogle, the Isabelle AFP at title/abstract/filename level, Coq, HOL Light, Metamath, arXiv; GitHub native code search and Mizar not run) the entry is not aware of a prior formalization of Salem's theorem or of Salem numbers in any surveyed prover ecosystem; the one adjacent hit is the IsPisot definition in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (the definition and the golden-ratio instance; no Salem numbers), whose spelling the compared statement adopts. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

records.title: Nash's isometric embedding theorem for closed manifolds (Günther's proof)
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Nash's C^∞ isometric embedding theorem for closed manifolds: every compact smooth manifold without boundary, equipped with a smooth Riemannian metric, admits a smooth injective map into some Euclidean space ℝ^q whose differential pulls the Euclidean inner product back to the given metric. The proof formalized is Günther's (1989), which replaces the Nash-Moser iteration by an elliptic fixed-point argument, following the presentation in A. J. Wassermann's Cambridge Part III lecture notes as the primary source. The development has two layers. The first proves the theorem for the flat torus: a self-contained Sobolev toolkit on 𝕋ⁿ (weighted ℓ² Sobolev spaces on ℤⁿ, Rellich compactness, the Sobolev sup bound, three multiplication theorems, mollifiers, periodization, Fourier inversion and Parseval), the approximation of smooth metrics by realizable ones, Günther's perturbation theorem proved by a contraction in Hˢ, and their assembly into the statement that every smooth 2π-periodic positive-definite matrix field on ℝⁿ is the pullback metric of a smooth periodic immersion that is injective modulo 2πℤⁿ. The second layer reduces the closed-manifold case to the torus: a Whitney embedding from Mathlib is extended to the ambient space, the metric is extended by a pseudo-inverse construction, cut off, symmetrized and periodized, and the torus theorem is applied. No bound on the embedding dimension is claimed. Concrete instances (round spheres of every dimension, products of spheres, the flat torus 𝕊¹ × 𝕊¹) are derived, and the flat-torus instance is shown to reproduce the torus theorem's conclusion, tying the two layers together. Nothing here is claimed to be new.

records.title: The De Bruijn–Erdős Theorem on Incidence Geometry and Near-Pencil Tightness
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the De Bruijn–Erdős theorem (1948) in incidence geometry and pairwise balanced block designs, together with its constructive near-pencil tightness proof. Proves that any finite linear space on n ≥ 3 non-collinear points determines at least n lines (|P| ≤ |L|) via the classical combinatorial double-counting inequality. Furthermore, explicitly constructs the near-pencil configuration with designated apex p₀ (consisting of one line of n - 1 points and n - 1 lines of 2 points) and proves that it forms a valid linear space achieving exact equality |L| = |P|. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: Erdős Problem 625: chromatic versus cochromatic number of a random graph
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the full-sequence quantitative theorem for G(n,1/2): with probability tending to one, the chromatic number minus the cochromatic number is at least ((log 2)^2/4) log(200/153) times n/(log n)^3. The formal statement uses the finite binomial random-graph measure, natural-valued chromatic and cochromatic numbers, real subtraction, and convergence along all natural n.

records.title: Levi–Civita connections and metric-determined curvature invariants in Lean
records.abstract: Formalizes a coherent static Riemannian theorem family for smooth finite-dimensional manifolds: existence of a global C^1 Levi–Civita covariant derivative, independence of the bundled curvature tensor from the chosen Levi–Civita realization, symmetry of the Ricci contraction, and independence of both Ricci and scalar curvature from that realization. These are standard classical results assembled at the current Mathlib manifold/vector-bundle API boundary. The contribution claimed here is a kernel-checked Lean formalization of the theorem family and its bundled constructions, not a new mathematical discovery or a priority claim.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: An explicit periodic signing of C_n(1,2) below the conjectured minimum
records.abstract: The paper's disproof of Suvagiya's signed-circulant minimum conjecture on an infinite arithmetic progression, formalized at the matrix level. For every n divisible by 8, Lean defines the paper's period-8 triangle-flux signing of the circulant graph C_n(1,2) as an explicit signed adjacency matrix, proves it is a plus-minus-one signing of mathlib's circulant graph, and proves by exact rational sum-of-squares window certificates that every eigenvalue has absolute value at most 1397/500. For every n >= 32 this rational separator lies strictly below the conjectured minimum rho_-(n) = 2*sqrt(cos^2(pi/n)+cos^2(2pi/n)), so the conjectured value is beaten by an explicit signing on all of n = 0 mod 8, n >= 32. The full Bloch determinant identity and the all-phase algebraic band-edge certificate remain selected as the supporting layer.

records.title: Mean Value for Random Ideal Lattices: Lean formalization
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the geometric, analytic, and arithmetic argument for mean values of lattice-point counts in Haar-random unit-covolume ideal lattices. For cyclotomic fields, it proves the conditional quantitative estimate for every exponent below the assumed subconvexity exponent and its positive power-saving corollary, uniformly over origin-centered balls. The subconvexity, Stark residue, and discriminant-growth inputs remain explicit hypotheses rather than claimed consequences of the formalization.

records.title: The Kőnig–Egerváry Theorem on Matchings and Vertex Covers in Bipartite Graphs
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of the Kőnig–Egerváry Theorem (1931) and Gallai identities (1959). Proves strong min-max duality matchingNumber(G) = vertexCoverNumber(G) for 2-colorable graphs G via Hall's defect matching theorem, and formalizes Gallai's identity independenceNumber(G) + vertexCoverNumber(G) = |V(G)|. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: A machine-checked bound of 0.6934 for Besicovitch's 1/2-problem
records.abstract:
Besicovitch's 1/2-conjecture asserts that a Borel set in the plane with finite one-dimensional Hausdorff measure whose lower density exceeds 1/2 almost everywhere is countably 1-rectifiable. Writing sigma_1(R^2) for the least threshold that forces countable 1-rectifiability, the conjecture is sigma_1(R^2) = 1/2. The previously published record is sigma_1(R^2) <= 7/10, obtained by De Lellis, Glaudo, Massaccesi and Vittone.
This development proves, with a complete Lean 4 proof term, sigma_1(R^2) <= 6934/10000 = 0.6934.

records.title: heilbronn-convex-3-8
records.abstract:
For n = 3 through n = 8, this formalization determines the supremal minimum triangle area among n indexed planar points whose own convex hull has Lebesgue area one. It proves a pointwise upper bound, attainment, and the exact value for every n in that range. The values are 1, 1/2, (5-sqrt(5))/10, 1/6, 1/9, and, at n = 8, the unique root in (79/1000, 81/1000) of 2060x^5 - 2332x^4 + 1064x^3 - 240x^2 + 26x - 1.
For n = 3, 4, 5, 6, and 8 it also proves pairwise uniqueness of optimizers modulo arbitrary relabeling and arbitrary nonsingular affine transformations. Uniqueness is false at n = 7; instead, an explicit real family is proved to attain throughout its full parameter interval and to exhaust all unit-hull optimizers up to the same equivalence. A real subinterval is pairwise inequivalent, exhibiting a continuum-parameterized set of optimizer orbits; an explicit countable subfamily is retained too.
The n = 3 and n = 4 cases are elementary folklore. The sharp n = 6 and n = 7 values were published by Dress-Yang-Zeng and Yang-Zeng, respectively; the Lean developments here independently reprove those results rather than formalizing the published arguments. The full n = 5 result, the explicit n = 7 family and optimizer classification, and the exact n = 8 result and optimizer classification are first presented in this development. The scoped search described below located prior candidate records but no published full n = 5 proof, no prior exhaustive n = 7 optimizer classification, and no published n = 8 proof. This is not an absolute priority claim. These results are intended for researchers in discrete and computational geometry studying extremal configurations, exact geometric bounds, and formalized combinatorial geometry.

records.title: Chip-Firing with Lean 4
records.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Baker and Norine's Riemann-Roch theorem for finite graphs. Chip configurations on a finite graph, modulo chip-firing moves, form an abelian group analogous to the group of line bundles on a compact Riemann surface. Each class can be assigned a rank, analogous to the dimension of a linear series. These ranks then satisfy a formula of the form r(D) - r(K-D) = deg D + 1 - g, in exact analogy to Riemann surfaces. This formula is formalized, along with the analog of Clifford's theorem for finite graphs.

records.title: The trace form of a tensor product of algebras and the signature product rule, with the trace forms of Q[x]/(x^3 - x - 1), Q[x]/(x^4 - x - 1) and their compositum as instances
records.abstract: GENERAL THEOREMS FIRST. For finite free algebras A, B over a commutative ring R, the trace form of the tensor product A ⊗_R B is the tensor product of the trace forms, and over a linearly ordered field the Sylvester signature of a tensor product of quadratic forms obeys a product rule. Seven compared general statements: (1) the trace of a pure tensor is the product of the traces, Tr_{A⊗B}(a ⊗ b) = Tr_A(a)·Tr_B(b); (2) the trace form on pure tensors is the product of the trace forms; (3) the Gram matrix of a tensor basis bA ⊗ bB (Mathlib's Basis.tensorProduct) is the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices; (4) the discriminant product formula WITH SIGN, disc(bA ⊗ bB) = disc(bA)^|kappa| · disc(bB)^|iota| for bases indexed by finite types iota, kappa; (5) when 2 is invertible in R, the trace quadratic form of A ⊗ B is the tensor product (Mathlib's QuadraticForm.tmul) of the trace quadratic forms; (6)-(7) THE SIGNATURE PRODUCT RULE: over a linearly ordered field with 2 invertible, for quadratic forms Q1, Q2 on finite-dimensional spaces, sigPos(Q1 ⊗ Q2) = p1 p2 + n1 n2 and sigNeg(Q1 ⊗ Q2) = p1 n2 + n1 p2, with sigPos/sigNeg Mathlib's basis-free invariants (maximal dimension of a positive- resp. negative-definite subspace). (6)-(7) are the (p, n)-refinement of the multiplicativity of the signature homomorphism on the Witt ring of an ordered field (Lam 2005, Chapter VIII), stated for arbitrary (possibly degenerate) forms and proved by orthogonal bases and the uniqueness half of Sylvester's law. The Witt-ring statement gives only the difference p - n; recovering p and n separately for a possibly degenerate tensor product would in addition need the dimension of the radical of a tensor product, which Mathlib does not have either; the entry proves the two counts directly, without the Witt ring, which is not formalized. None of (1)-(7) was in Mathlib at the pin; Mathlib's nearest results are the trace of a tensor product of endomorphisms (LinearMap.trace_tensorProduct'), the determinant of a Kronecker product, the tensor product of quadratic forms and its polar form, orthogonal bases, and sigPos/sigNeg with Sylvester uniqueness — the infrastructure from which (1)-(7) are built. PRIOR ART on (4): Mathlib at the pin has NumberField.natAbs_discr_eq_natAbs_discr_pow_mul_natAbs_discr_pow — for two linearly disjoint number fields with coprime different ideals the ABSOLUTE VALUE of the discriminant of their compositum is |d1|^[K2:Q]·|d2|^[K1:Q] (via the different; the classical statement is in Khanduja 2019). Statement (4) is the elementary basis-level version: any finite free algebras over any commutative ring, the exact signed discriminant of the tensor basis, with no number-field, integrality or coprimality hypothesis; it neither implies nor is implied by the Mathlib theorem, and is cited beside it. THE INSTANCES (8)-(23), at the two fields cut out by the trinomials x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 — the cubic and quartic members of the family x^n - x - 1, irreducible over the rationals for every n >= 2 by Selmer's theorem (Mathlib), whose real roots above 1 are the plastic number and the quartic root of x^4 = x + 1 — and their compositum. The trace form of a number field K of degree n is (x, y) -> Tr(xy); in the power basis 1, x, ..., x^(n-1) its Gram matrix is the Hankel matrix (Tr x^(i+j)) of the power sums of the roots. (8)-(9) The Gram matrices, entrywise: Algebra.traceMatrix of the power family equals the explicit integer Hankel matrix — power sums 3, 0, 2, 3, 2 for the cubic and 4, 0, 0, 3, 4, 0, 3 for the quartic, from Newton's identities on the coefficients. (10)-(11) The discriminants of the power bases, Algebra.discr of the same families: -23 and -283, both prime. (12)-(13) Explicit diagonalisations: the trace form, as a quadratic form, is equivalent to the weighted sum of squares with weights 3, 2, -23/6 resp. 4, 4, -9/4, 283/36 — one congruence among many, exhibited with its rational change of basis. (14)-(17) The Sylvester signatures as basis-free invariants: sigPos and sigNeg are 2 and 1 for the cubic trace form and 3 and 1 for the quartic, read off from (12)-(13) through Sylvester uniqueness. (18)-(23) THE COMPOSITUM: the tensor product L = K_3 ⊗_Q K_4 is their compositum Q(rho, Q) — the degrees 3 and 4 are coprime, so the fields are linearly disjoint and L is a field, statement (23), from Mathlib's coprime-degree linear-disjointness criterion — and (18)-(22) are the general theorems at this pair: Tr(x ⊗ y) = Tr(x)·Tr(y); the Gram matrix of the tensor power family x^i ⊗ y^j (Fin 3 × Fin 4) is the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices; the discriminant of that family is (-23)^4·(-283)^3 by (4); the Sylvester signature is (7, 5) by (6)-(7) applied to (2, 1) and (3, 1) — agreeing with the classical (r_1 + r_2, r_2) for the compositum's two real and five complex places (context, not compared). The registered compositum entry PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005 treats the same field as Q(rho·Q), through the degree-12 minimal polynomial of the product; that Q(rho, Q) = Q(rho·Q) follows by degree count and is context here, never compared. THE CLASSICAL SETTING of the instances: the trace form of a number field with r_1 real and r_2 pairs of complex embeddings has signature (r_1 + r_2, r_2) — for the Hankel form of a polynomial this is Hermite's 1856 theorem (the signature difference counts the distinct real roots), and for the discriminant matrix of a number field it is Taussky's 1968 note; Conner and Perlis's 1984 survey is the standard reference. Here (r_1, r_2) = (1, 1), (2, 1) and (2, 5), so the classical theorem predicts exactly (2, 1), (3, 1) and (7, 5), and the Hermite counts 2 - 1 = 1 and 3 - 1 = 2 match the real-root counts of the two trinomials. That general theorem is NOT formalized: the two-field instances are proved directly by explicit congruence, the compositum instance by the general theorems (1)-(7); the embedding counts r_1, r_2 appear in no compared statement. WHY THESE FIELDS, for the instances: the cubic field is the signature-[1, 1] cubic field of smallest absolute discriminant (LMFDB, sorted by |disc|: 3.1.23.1 first, then 3.1.31.1); its Galois closure is the Artin field of the weight-one newform 23.1.b.a = eta(z) eta(23z), the classical Hecke example with Artin image S_3, whose analytic conductor the LMFDB records as minimal among all classical newforms and whose Stark unit is the root of x^3 - x - 1 itself; its integral trace form — which the compared Gram matrix (8) is, the power basis being an integral basis — is the object of Mantilla-Soler's study of integral trace forms of cubic fields (Algebra & Number Theory 2010). The quartic field is the degree-4 member of the same trinomial family, registered as the degree-4 Mahler-measure minimizer (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004), with the same profile: prime discriminant, monogenic. The field discriminants: the LMFDB records 4.2.283.1 (defining polynomial x^4 - x - 1, signature [2, 1], discriminant -283, monogenic, index 1) and 3.1.23.1 (reduced defining polynomial x^3 - x^2 + 1, the field generated by -1/rho, signature [1, 1], discriminant -23, monogenic, index 1) list -283 and -23 as the field discriminants; that the power bases are integral bases, so that the compared power-basis discriminants ARE the field discriminants, is cited from those records and not formalized; likewise the tensor power family is an integral basis of the compositum because the two discriminants are coprime (the standard integral-basis theorem for linearly disjoint fields; context only). PRIOR ART on the instances, as of the 2026-09-02 sweep: Mathlib contains no trace-form or discriminant computation for either field. The nearest prior work is the Lean 4 certification framework of Baanen, Chavarri Villarello and Dahmen (CPP 2025) and its 2026 sequel (Chavarri Villarello and Dahmen): they certify rings of integers, FIELD discriminants (as the determinant of the trace matrix of a certified integral basis) and, in the sequel, the signature (r_1, r_2) by real-root counting, for LMFDB entries at large; neither treats the trace form's Sylvester signature, and their published example sets (seven non-monogenic cubic fields unramified outside 2, 3, 5 in the first; the v1 example directory of the second) contain neither of the two fields here (checked 2026-09-02). Relative to that work, the compared discriminants (10)-(11) are the power-basis discriminants derived from the explicit Gram matrices — a weaker notion than the certified field discriminant, which coincides with it here because both fields are monogenic (LMFDB, cited) — and the Sylvester signatures have no counterpart there. The entry is not aware of a formalization, in any surveyed prover ecosystem, of the trace form of a tensor product of algebras, of the signature product rule, or of a number field's trace-form Sylvester signature. The proof modules descend from the author's public pdt-lean development (pinned below), where none of these statements was ever a compared statement. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

records.title: Ore's and Dirac's Theorems on Hamiltonian Cycles
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Ore's theorem (1960) and Dirac's theorem (1952) on the existence of Hamiltonian cycles in simple graphs. Proves Ore's degree-sum condition via maximal path cycle-closure and connectivity arguments, and derives Dirac's minimum-degree theorem as a corollary. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: A proof of Conway's refinement conjecture
records.abstract: A Lean proof of Conway's 1976 refinement conjecture for omnific integers. For omnific integers a, b, c, d with ab = cd, it proves the existence of omnific integers e, f, g, h satisfying a = ef, b = gh, c = eg, and d = fh, including zero and degenerate cases. The proof proceeds through factorisation and refinement theory for generalised-power-series integer parts and connects the generalised-power-series and surreal-number formulations.

records.title: Tverberg's Partition Theorem, 1D Theorem, and Colorful 1D Theorem
records.abstract: A complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Tverberg's Theorem (Helge Tverberg, 1966) in the distinct-point set formulation across dimensions d >= 1 (with d = 0, r > 1 cases vacuously satisfied due to Finset carrier capacity limits on Fin 0 -> ℝ) via the Sarkaria–Bárány Colorful Carathéodory reduction, the full 1D Tverberg theorem for arbitrary r via symmetric-rank pairing following Mulzer–Werner, and the 1-dimensional Colorful Tverberg Theorem for arbitrary r (Bárány–Larman–Pach 1992). Proves that any (r - 1)(d + 1) + 1 points in ℝ^d can be partitioned into r parts whose convex hulls intersect, and that two disjoint color classes of r points each in ℝ¹ can be partitioned into r colorful pairs whose convex hulls share a common point of intersection. To the maintainers' knowledge, the theorem was not found in an exact declaration name, docstring, and type signature search of the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1).

records.title: Radial harmonic functions on a real inner product space: the classification, the Laplacian of radial functions, and the stability of circular orbits for power-law central forces; Ehrenfest's dimensionality argument (1917) as the application
records.abstract: GENERAL THEOREMS FIRST. Throughout, E is a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension n, Δ is Mathlib's coordinate-free Laplacian, HarmonicOnNhd its harmonic functions, and f : ℝ → ℝ is twice differentiable on (0, ∞) (two HasDerivAt hypotheses, with derivatives f', f''). (I) THE CLASSIFICATION OF RADIAL HARMONIC FUNCTIONS: (1) for n ≠ 2 and E ≠ 0, the radial function f ∘ ‖·‖ is harmonic on E ∖ {0} if and only if f(r) = a + b r^(2−n) on (0, ∞) for some real a, b; (2) for n = 2, if and only if f(r) = a + b log r — every radial harmonic function with a twice-differentiable profile is an affine function of the Newtonian potential, constants included, and of the logarithm in the plane. (II) THE LAPLACIAN OF RADIAL FUNCTIONS, away from the origin: (3) Δ(f ∘ ‖·‖)(x) = f''(‖x‖) + (n − 1) f'(‖x‖)/‖x‖, the radial Laplacian; (4) for g twice differentiable on (0, ∞), Δ(g(‖y‖²))(x) = 2n g'(‖x‖²) + 4‖x‖² g''(‖x‖²), the squared-norm parametrization; (5) for every real s, Δ(‖y‖^s)(x) = s (n + s − 2) ‖x‖^(s−2), the indicial identity (its consequence, not itself compared: for E ≠ 0, ‖y‖^s is harmonic away from 0 exactly when s (n + s − 2) = 0, at s = 0 and s = 2 − n, which coincide at n = 2); (6) Δ(log ‖y‖)(x) = (n − 2)/‖x‖²; (7) ‖y‖^(2−n) is harmonic on E ∖ {0} for every n — for n ≥ 3, up to its normalizing constant, the Newtonian kernel away from the origin (the normalization and the distributional identity −ΔΦ = δ at the origin, in Evans's sign convention, which make a normalized multiple of it the fundamental solution proper, are NOT formalized); at n = 2 the power is the constant 1 and the logarithmic case is (8); on the zero space the statement is vacuous; (8) log ‖y‖ is harmonic on E ∖ {0} when n = 2. (III) THE RADIAL EQUATION, the one-variable content of (1)-(2): (9) for n ≠ 2, f'' + (n − 1) f'/r = 0 on (0, ∞) if and only if f(r) = a + b r^(2−n) there for some a, b; (10) for n = 2, if and only if f(r) = a + b log r. (IV) THE STABILITY OF CIRCULAR ORBITS, general in the real exponent: for the effective potential U(r) = a/r² − b/r^p on (0, ∞), a, b > 0, p > 0 real — the radial potential of a body with angular momentum under a central attraction with force law 1/r^(p+1) — (11) U'(r) = 0 iff r^(2−p) = 2a/(bp), the circular-orbit condition (for p ≠ 2 that equation has exactly one positive solution, whence "the circular orbit" below — a consequence of (11), not itself compared; in the plane "the circular orbit r = √(2a/b)" names the point of (19)); (12) at a circular orbit U''(r) = 2a(2 − p)/r⁴; (13) for p < 2 the circular orbit r* = (2a/(bp))^(1/(2−p)) is a local minimum of U (Mathlib's non-strict IsLocalMin) — stable; (14) for p > 2 it is a local maximum — unstable; (15) for p > 2 U has no local minimum on (0, ∞) at all (Ehrenfest's reading, that bounded motion between two radii is then impossible, is not formalized); (16) U''(r*) r*⁴/(2a) = 2 − p, the square of the ratio of the radial to the angular frequency of small oscillations about the circular orbit, which the local step of Bertrand's argument requires to be the square of a rational number for a near-circular orbit to close. The boundary p = 2, where the two terms of U have the same power, is covered by the critical-point and second-derivative identities (11)-(12), whose only hypothesis on the exponent is p > 0, and is excluded from the stability conclusions (13)-(15) and the frequency identity (16), all of which require p ≠ 2; among the instances it is n = 4, where (17) with a ≠ b yields no local minimum (the potential (a − b)/r² has no critical point) while the sub-case a = b, where U vanishes, is excluded; the table's 'unstable' cell at n = 4 is not compared. THE INSTANCES (17)-(23), with p = n − 2 for the Newtonian potential in n ≥ 3 dimensions and the logarithmic potential in the plane: (17) for n ≥ 3 and a ≠ b a stable circular orbit exists iff n = 3 (a ≠ b excludes n = 4, a = b, where U vanishes identically and every point is a non-strict minimum); (18) for n ≥ 5 the effective potential has no local minimum on (0, ∞); (19) in the plane, for a/r² + b log r, the circular orbit r = √(2a/b) is stable; (20) the quantity of (16) is 4 − n for n ≥ 3, n ≠ 4, hence 1 at n = 3; (21) in the plane it equals 2; (22) in the plane its square root is irrational (it is √2 by (21); this statement asserts irrationality only); (23) ‖x‖^(2−n) is harmonic on ℝⁿ ∖ {0} for every n; for n ≥ 3, up to its normalizing constant, the Newtonian kernel away from the origin, with the same disclosure as (7). THE APPLICATION: Ehrenfest's argument of 1917 (KNAW Proceedings 20 (1918) 200-209, §1 and Appendix I) that the stability of planetary orbits singles out three spatial dimensions. He deduces the n-dimensional force law from the Laplace–Poisson equation (the Laplace half is statement (7), harmonicity away from the source; the Poisson half, the point source, is not formalized; the classification (1)-(2) makes "the radial harmonic function" a theorem), reduces the motion to the radial equation ṙ = (1/r)√(A r² + B r^(4−n) − C²), and tabulates three columns — circular trajectories; motions between two positive values of r; motion to the infinite — for n ≥ 4 (unstable, impossible, possible), n = 3 (stable, possible and moreover closed, possible), n = 2 (stable, possible and not closed, impossible). Statements (17)-(22) are the extrema and frequency identities of the effective potential behind the first two columns for n ≥ 5, n = 3, n = 2 — a local minimum where the table says stable, no local minimum where it says bounded motion is impossible, the frequency ratio where it says closed or not closed; the passage from those identities to trajectories (bounded motion, closure, the third column), the n = 4 cell, and Bertrand's global theorem (1873) are not formalized. Tangherlini (1963) extended the argument to the n-dimensional Schwarzschild field; Caruso and Xavier (1987) and Tegmark (1997) discuss its epistemological status and call it Ehrenfest's argument, as does this entry ("Ehrenfest's theorem" names his 1927 quantum-mechanical result). NOT formalized: Bertrand's theorem, the third column and the n = 4 cell of the table, the derivation of the effective potential from the equations of motion, the relativistic extension, the wave-equation half of Ehrenfest's paper (Huygens' principle in odd dimensions), and any statement about the actual dimension of physical space — the theorems classify radial functions and a family of effective potentials; the reading that the stable case is the world we observe is Ehrenfest's, cited, not compared. PRIOR ART, as of the 2026-09-02 sweep: Mathlib has the Laplacian on inner product spaces (InnerProductSpace.laplacian, laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis), harmonic functions (HarmonicAt, HarmonicOnNhd, harmonicAt_congr_nhds) with complex-analytic examples — in particular AnalyticAt.harmonicAt_log_norm, which gives log |z| harmonic on ℂ ∖ {0}, the n = 2 case of (8) in the complex model obtained through complex analysis — the second- derivative test (isLocalMin_of_deriv_deriv_pos), the mean-value lemmas IsOpen.exists_is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero and IsOpen.exists_eq_add_of_deriv_eq, and real powers; it has no Laplacian of a radial function, no harmonic power of the norm, no classification of radial harmonic functions, no central-force mechanics, and no formalization of Ehrenfest's argument. No formalization of the classification of radial harmonic functions, of Ehrenfest's argument, of the harmonic Newtonian potential in general dimension, or of Bertrand's theorem was found in the surveyed prover ecosystems (Mathlib and its archive, the Isabelle AFP, the Coq Mathematical Components and Coquelicot analysis libraries). The proof module descends from the author's public pdt-lean development (pinned below), where none of these statements was ever a compared statement. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.

records.title: Sharp bounds for intervals in finite subgroup lattices
records.abstract: Let H be a subgroup of a finite group G, let n = [G:H] > 1, and let p be the least prime divisor of n. This Lean development proves an exact finite rational upper envelope for the number of subgroups K with H ≤ K ≤ G and the strict bound c(p) n^((log_p n)/4), where c(p) is an Euler-product times a Gaussian theta series. It formalizes the bandwise moment inequality that drives the proof, a universal base-two bound with an exact decimal coefficient, the exact optimal answer for prime-power indices, and elementary-abelian asymptotics showing that both the constant and the exponent 1/4 are optimal.

records.title: Erdős Problem 684: f(n)/log n is unbounded — a Lean 4 formalization of arXiv:2604.23784
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, against Mathlib, of the main theorem of J. H. Bae, "Unbounded logarithmic limsup in Erdős Problem 684 via shifted carry scheduling" (arXiv:2604.23784, v3).  For 0 ≤ k ≤ n write C(n,k) = u·v with u supported on the primes ≤ k and v on the primes in (k,n], and let f(n) be the least k with u > n²; Erdős asked for bounds on f(n) (Problem 684 in Bloom's database).  The compared theorems state that for every ε > 0 there are infinitely many n with f(n) > (1/2 − ε)·log n·log log n / log log log n, equivalently limsup f(n)·log log log n /(log n·log log n) ≥ 1/2 (stated in the extended nonnegative reals), and in particular that f(n)/log n is unbounded, so no estimate f(n) = O(log n) holds.  This strengthens the subsequential lower bound (1/2 − o(1)) log n of Alexeev–Putterman–Sawhney–Sellke–Valiant by a factor of order log log n / log log log n; the general upper bound (log n)² remains the best known and the exact order of f(n) is open.  Two further compared statements fix the meaning of the definitions: u(n,k) times the part of C(n,k) supported on primes exceeding k equals C(n,k), and K < f(n) holds exactly when u(n,k) ≤ n² for all 1 ≤ k ≤ min(K,n).  The proof follows the paper section by section (Kummer carries, a product-cell code, a CRT count with exponential weighting, an anchored-fibre selection lemma, and a four-range carry budget).  The prime number theorem is the single analytic input: the library proves the theorem under the explicit hypothesis θ(x) = x + O(x/log² x) and then discharges that hypothesis from the bound ψ(x) = x + O(x·exp(−c(log x)^{1/10})) of the PrimeNumberTheoremAnd project (Kontorovich, Tao et al.), so the compared theorems carry no hypotheses and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Tucker's Lemma: Full Combinatorial & Topological Parity Suite in 1D and 2D
records.abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Tucker's Lemma (Albert W. Tucker, 1945) and the combinatorial Borsuk–Ulam theorem in 1D and 2D without artificial conditions. Formalizes four foundational pillars: (1) 1D discrete sign-change parity and antipodal interval subdivision lemma; (2) 2D combinatorial double counting of face doors and modulo-2 parity conservation on edge-pseudomanifolds; (3) the boundary cycle engine on 2D edge-pseudomanifolds with an enumerated cyclic boundary (CyclicBoundaryPseudomanifold2D) under antipodal boundary labeling, proving that non-complementary boundary labelings force odd boundary door parity, thereby establishing the 2D Tucker's Lemma on cyclic boundary pseudomanifolds, retracting previous claims of full topological disk coverage; and (4) the concrete 6-vertex, 8-face, 12-edge octahedral 2-sphere S^2_8 triangulation. All declarations rely strictly on standard Lean 4 kernel axioms (propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice).

records.title: Even-order Grünschloß–Keller permutation nets: net property and tiling distance
records.abstract: This Lean development proves that the even-order permutation construction of Grünschloß and Keller (MCQMC 2008 proceedings, implemented in gendiag0m2.h) is a base-2 (0,m,2)-net for every even m >= 4. The proof is symbolic: for every resolution a <= m the dyadic-box map is shown injective through the concatenation x = floor(k/4) + 2^(m/2-2) z and fixed-width bit-reversal splitting, and a cardinality argument upgrades injectivity to a bijection (exactly one point per elementary interval). For the source's row-shifted tiling lattice <(N,0),(N/4,N)> it proves, for every even m >= 8, that one explicit pair of points has squared distance 241 * 2^(m-8), and at m = 8 that 241 is the exact minimum over all pairs and all lattice translates. The exhaustive m = 8 lower bound is reduced by ordinary kernel decide; the exactness of the computed candidate minimum over the whole lattice is a symbolic lemma. The all-parameter lower bound of the distance theorem (even m >= 10) is proved in the paper but is not formalized.

records.title: Combinatorial core of the K₃,₃,₁-redundancy theorem for tetrahedral balls
records.abstract: Alexa's three-dimensional Tutte embedding theorem (Discrete & Computational Geometry, 2025) requires the graph of a tetrahedral mesh to have neither a K₆ nor a K₃,₃,₁ minor and asks whether the second exclusion is necessary. The paper proves that it is redundant for finite simplicial complexes whose realization is a closed topological 3-ball and which satisfy the boundary-triangle condition (BT): if the 1-skeleton G has no K₆ minor, then G is linklessly embeddable and hence has no K₃,₃,₁ minor (Theorem 1.1). This Lean development proves the paper's new combinatorial mathematics over mathlib simple graphs and finite simplicial complexes and composes it into Theorem 1.1 with the cited theorems as explicit hypotheses. Proved: for every four-clique of a (BT) pair the induced relative F₂ chain complex has homology of dimension at most one (Lemma 4.3, with the soundness of its Boolean coordinate model, Lemma 7.1); a K₄-attachment never merges components of the old part (Lemma 5.2); every MP₁-cockade whose four-clique deletions leave at most two components is linklessly embeddable, given the four-clique Holst–Lovász–Schrijver criterion and linkless atoms (Proposition 5.3); and the joined statement structural_theorem, in which the skeleton of the complex is a mathlib SimpleGraph, every skeleton four-clique is a labelled four-clique of the pair, and the hypotheses are Corollary 3.6 (rigidity, Mader, Jørgensen), the relative ball duality of Section 4, Corollary 2.5, and Lemma 5.1. Generic rigidity, the extremal-minor classification, PL duality, the Holst–Lovász–Schrijver theorem, apex linklessness, and Alexa's theorem are not formalized and enter only as named hypotheses.

records.title: A kernel-checked exclusion certificate for Erdős Problem 647, to 10^8
records.abstract:
Erdős Problem 647 asks whether there is any n > 24 with max_{m < n} (m + tau(m)) <= n + 2, where tau counts divisors. The value n = 24 satisfies it and the question is open. This entry certifies a bounded exclusion: no such n exists in (24, 10^8]. It does not resolve the problem and asserts nothing about n > 10^8.
The exclusion is certified rather than searched at check time. A witness at a cover position is an offset together with prime-power pairs dividing m, certifying tau(m) >= prod (e + 1); every prime in a pair is below 1024 and is checked prime by eleven trial divisions, so no primality certificates appear anywhere. A chain of witnesses covers the interval and each certificate chunk is discharged by a single decide against the chain checker, so the Lean kernel certifies the arithmetic and the generator that produced it is never trusted.
The audience is the community working on the Erdős problems database and its Lean formalizations, for whom a machine-checked lower bound on the search range is directly usable, and researchers building certificate-based exclusions in elementary number theory, for whom the witness format and its kernel-evaluable checkers are the transferable part.

records.title: Sharp arithmetic separation in chiral Padovan histories
records.abstract: Sixteen compared statements establish quantitative recurrence for the actual infinite Padovan prefix path and compare cubic and quartic arithmetic record windows. For 0<epsilon<=1, every nonempty prefix whose conjugate coordinate lies within epsilon of the origin has expanding coordinate at least epsilon^(-2); an actual prefix returns with expanding coordinate at most r^3*epsilon^(-2). Every letter stream satisfies the pairwise bound abs(Delta X)*norm(Delta W)^2>=1, and Padovan substitution stages attain equality at arbitrarily large clocks. The full cubic record window is relatively dense with uniformly discrete differences; the identical positive-real window in the quartic case admits nonzero inverse-unit points arbitrarily close to zero, while its other real embedding grows. Scalar prefix coordinates factor the included faithful chiral timelike history in the genuine quartic trace geometry. The formalization exposes the return bounds, actual-word attainment, constructive covering, and explicit obstruction as its principal mathematical consequences.

records.title: Carlet's Kasami cyclic-additive conjecture
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of the Kasami cyclic-additive conjecture introduced by Claude Carlet. For the derivative image of the Kasami monomial x^(4^k-2^k+1) with gcd(k,n)=1, over a finite field of characteristic two with 2^n elements, the formalized result gives the exact three-variable coefficient count 2^(2n-3) for every pair of distinct nonzero coefficients.

records.title: Brill--Noether generality and gonality for chains of cycles and theta graphs
records.abstract: This repository formalizes Brill--Noether generality for chains whose factors may be cycles or theta graphs, subject to a genericity condition on path lengths and an evenly-marked condition on the theta factors. A graph is called Brill--Noether general if the possible degrees and ranks of its chip configurations, in the sense of Baker and Norine, match the behavior of a general algebraic curve. Here we use only the existential form of Brill--Noether generality, without computing dimensions. Following Cools--Draisma--Payne--Robeva, we also formalize a mild vanishing-order condition that permits the recovery of dimension statements on the algebraic side. A Brill--Noether general graph also has the conjectural maximum gonality in its genus. The chain of cycles case is a theorem of Cools--Draisma--Payne--Robeva, which Pflueger--Solomon generalized to allow evenly-marked theta graphs. Among other things, the construction shows the existence, in every positive genus g, of graphs with every gonality between 2 and ceil(g/2) + 1, inclusive.

records.title: The optimal universal exponential base for Euclidean kissing numbers
records.abstract: For every positive integer n, the Euclidean kissing number tau_n is an attained maximum and satisfies tau_n <= (sqrt(6))^n. This Lean formalization proves the bound by packing explicit bodies of revolution in the unit ball, including the geometric separation, volume integrals, and every dimension case. An explicit six-point planar configuration proves tau_2 = 6. Consequently sqrt(6) is the least nonnegative (and least positive) universal exponential base without a prefactor; the admissible bases are exactly alpha >= sqrt(6), and the supremum of tau_n^(1/n) over positive dimensions equals sqrt(6). No asymptotic-optimality claim is made.

records.title: N4Code: optimal finite-length block codes of size four for binary symmetric channels
records.abstract: A Lean 4 and mathlib formalization of the Dong-Yang classification of optimal (n,4) binary block codes for binary symmetric channels.  The registered results are Theorems 1-5 of the paper: existence of an optimal linear or Class-I code, the explicit linear optimal codes by residue class modulo 3, the universal strict-improvement reductions outside the linear, Class-I, and Class-II classes, the Class-I condition reduction to linear codes, and the finite classification for blocklengths 2 <= n <= 8. The Lean statements use the strict-improvement contrapositive forms.

records.title: Exact four-dimensional projection quality of the OneTwo Sobol' table at 65,536 points
records.abstract: The quality parameter t of a base-2 digital net with 2^m points measures exact equidistribution in dyadic boxes, and for Sobol' sequences used in quasi-Monte Carlo integration and computer graphics the quality of low-dimensional projections is a practical bottleneck. The OneTwo construction of Bonneel, Coeurjolly, Iehl, and Ostromoukhov (ACM Transactions on Graphics, 2025) releases a 692-dimension direction-number table whose protected pairs (2k-1, 2k) have the (1,2) property, with acceptance targets t <= 3 through m <= 10 and t <= 4 through m <= 15 for the pair-aligned four-dimensional blocks. Theorem 1.1 of the preprint determines the next depth exactly: at m = 16, a complete batch of 65,536 points, every one of the 345 pair-aligned windows of the released table has exact four-dimensional t-value 4 when its first dimension is one of 1, 7, 31, 49, 67, 195, 225, 243, 373 and t-value 5 otherwise, so the t <= 4 guarantee extends to m = 16 in exactly nine windows and fails in the other 336, each failure witnessed by an empty dyadic box of volume 2^-12 in that projection. The standard star-discrepancy bound for the projection is 299/4096 at t = 4 and 29/256 at t = 5. This Lean development proves the theorem in rank form with the released table embedded as one 256-bit literal per dimension: for every window, every four-part composition at the threshold total selects independent generator rows over F_2 and some composition one total higher does not, and the distribution is 9 windows at t = 4 and 336 at t = 5. The worked block, dimensions 25 to 28, keeps its separate explicit certificate (t = 5, with every smaller threshold refuted). All checks are 16-column XOR row reductions reduced by kernel decide with no native evaluation. The digital-net rank criterion, the discrepancy bound, and the authentication of the upstream table remain informal.

records.title: Li's criterion for the Riemann Hypothesis
records.abstract: Li's criterion for the Riemann zeta function, formalized in Lean 4 over Mathlib: Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis` holds if and only if every Li-Keiper coefficient of the completed xi function has nonnegative real part. The zero-indexed analytic coefficient at n is Li's classical lambda_(n+1), the n-th Taylor coefficient at 0 of the logarithmic derivative of s |-> xi(1/(1-s)). A second compared theorem identifies this analytic coefficient with Li's arithmetic coefficient, the symmetrized sum over the nontrivial zeros counted with multiplicity, and proves that symmetrized family summable so the sum is the genuine one. Both results are unconditional: the biconditional, the coefficient identification, the genus-1 Hadamard factorization of xi (with multiplicity), genus-1 summability of 1/|rho|^2, and the growth bound order(xi) <= 1 are all proved. This is a formalization of a classically known equivalence (X.-J. Li, 1997); it is not a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, nor of the positivity of the coefficients.

records.title: The global Kronecker–Weber theorem in Lean 4
records.abstract: This project formalizes the global Kronecker–Weber theorem in Lean 4: every finite abelian extension of the rational numbers embeds into a cyclotomic field. For a number field L that is abelian Galois over the rationals, the selected declaration gives a positive integer n and a rational algebra embedding from L into CyclotomicField n ℚ. The proof is supplied by the ClassFieldTheory library at a fixed commit, using Lean 4.33.0 and Mathlib.

records.title: Stafford 3.8
records.abstract: Lean formalization of Stafford's Conjecture 3.8 for every characteristic-zero field and every Weyl-algebra rank, proving that each nonzero d admits F, R, and S with 1 = d*R + F*d*S. The development also proves an exact Bernstein-degree fixed-source strengthening and derived localization, adjoint, and evolutionary results.

records.title: Convex geometry and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv problem: Theorem 1.2
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.2 of Dmitrii Zakharov's Convex geometry and the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv problem. For every fixed positive dimension d, as p tends to infinity through the primes, the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant s(F_p^d) satisfies s(F_p^d) = p w(F_p^d) + o(p), where w is the weak Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant.  Supporting proofs include the convex-flag Helly and centerpoint theorems, flag decomposition lemma, balanced convex combinations, relative set expansion, and the polynomial method bound for w. This submission covers Theorem 1.2 and its upper-bound formulation, not every result in the paper. The submission was prepared with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 / 6 Sol-Ultra under the direction and review of the author.  The GitHub page includes a PDF file zakharov_2026-3.pdf containing a revised version of the published paper generated  by ChatGPT 5.6 during this formalization project.  The only noteworthy difference is a correction to Definition 4.6 (Proper points) which was meant to use the function f^circ(q) in  place of \hat f(q) in the published version (this typo slipped in during one of the revision rounds of the paper). No other significant mistakes or corrections were discovered.

records.title: The sharp finite-field Nikodym exponent
records.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the sharp power saving in the finite-field Nikodym problem. A set N in F_q^d is a Nikodym set if through every point x there is a line all of whose points other than x lie in N. Lower bound: for every finite field F_q, every d >= 2 and every Nikodym set N in F_q^d, |N| >= q^d - (8 d^2 + 1) q^(d - 2^(1-d)); the proof goes through a carrier theorem for integral projective varieties containing many affine lines with private points, proved by finite-grid Hermite interpolation, Hilbert-function estimates (normalized monotonicity and a degree upper bound via linear Noether normalization), an interpolation cut, and a dimension induction that halves the saving at each step. Upper bound: for every d >= 2 and epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large primes q there is a Nikodym set N in F_q^d with |N| <= q^d - q^(d - 2^(1-d) - epsilon), constructed as the complement of a product set built from a totally real multiquadratic order in which q splits completely, with a digit encoding and tangent lines. Together these give Nik(d, q) = q^d - q^(d - 2^(1-d) + o(1)) along primes. Previously, for general q and d >= 3, the best lower bound was q^d / 2^(d-1) + O(q^(d-1)) and even Nik(d,q) = (1 - o(1)) q^d was open (Lund-Saraf-Wolf, Conjecture 2), while the best upper bounds for prime q were q^d - Omega_d(q^(d - eps_d)) with eps_d << 1/log log d and q^3 - Omega(q^2.1167) (Hunter-Pohoata-Verstraete-Zhang 2026); the lower bound here settles the former conjecture for every finite field, and the construction shows that the exponent d - 1/d conjectured by Chao and Yu (2026) is not sharp over prime fields. The README gives theorem-level comparisons and references. All three headline theorems are proved with no sorry and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.title: Spherical maximal functions: theorems of Stein and Bourgain
records.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of Stein's spherical maximal theorem and Bourgain's circular maximal theorem. The result concerns the sharp range of Lp boundedness of spherical maximal functions in Euclidean space and was first proved by Stein in dimensions three and greater. The much more subtle two-dimensional theorem was first proved by Bourgain. The proof of Bourgain's theorem in this formalization is via Mockenhaupt-Seeger-Sogge's classical argument via a local smoothing estimate for the wave equation. This required first  formalizing various underlying standard results from harmonic analysis. The final theorem statements were written by hand,  while the proofs were almost entirely machine-generated by coding agents with human supervision.

records.title: Double-contracted second Bianchi identity for metric-compatible torsion-free connections
records.abstract: Proves the orthonormal double contraction of the actual corrected curvature derivative of a tangent connection on a smooth finite-dimensional real manifold. The Challenge exposes the corrected commutator and the smooth tangent-vector extensions explicitly; the Solution proves the identity for every supplied extension satisfying the stated hypotheses. The derivative symmetries and cyclic Bianchi equations are derived from torsion-freeness and metric compatibility, not assumed as abstract tensor data. No separate Einstein-divergence theorem is selected.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

records.title: The density Hales–Jewett theorem and Szemerédi's theorem
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the density Hales–Jewett theorem: for every finite alphabet α and every density δ > 0, all sufficiently large n have the property that any set of at least δ·|α|^n words of length n over α contains a combinatorial line. The basis for the formalization is the combinatorial proof of Dodos, Kanellopoulos, and Tyros. As a consequence, we also formalize Szemerédi's theorem on the integers: for every k ≥ 3 and δ > 0, the following holds for all sufficiently large n. Any subset of {0, …, n−1} of size at least δ·n contains a nonconstant arithmetic progression of length k.

records.title: Marton's conjecture (the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture)
records.abstract: A Lean formalization of Marton's conjecture, widely known as the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture, together with its principal consequences. If A is a non-empty subset of an abelian group of exponent 2 with |A + A| <= K|A|, then A is covered by fewer than 2K^12 cosets of a subgroup of cardinality at most |A|; the same conclusion holds with 2K^9 cosets. For an abelian group in which mx = 0 for every x, with m >= 2, the covering number is m * K^(256m^3 + 1). Three consequences are also recorded: a finite set of small doubling in Z^D has a subset of at least K^(-34) of its size whose affine dimension is at most (80/log 2) log K; a map between finite groups of exponent 2 whose additive defects f(x+y) - f(x) - f(y) all lie in a set S differs from a homomorphism by a map taking at most |S|^10 values; and a map that is additive on at least a proportion 1/K of pairs agrees with a homomorphism on at least (|G| / (2^144 K^122) - 1)/2 points. The proofs are by an entropy method: one minimizes a functional of the entropic Ruzsa distance between two random variables and shows the minimum is attained at a uniform distribution on a subgroup, so the development also builds a substantial theory of Shannon entropy, entropic Ruzsa distance, and, for the bounded torsion case, a multidistance for m-tuples. The repository is a collaborative formalization project begun in November 2023; the mathematics is due to the cited papers and nothing here is claimed to be new. The compared theorems depend on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and on nothing else, and there is no sorry outside the six deliberate holes in PFRPalomar/Challenge.lean.

records.title: Subspace embeddings with the rerandomized SRHT
records.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of a rerandomized SRHT subspace embedding theorem. For every ambient Walsh dimension n = 2^m, rank 1 <= r <= n, and 0 < epsilon < 1, one deterministic width k <= min(n, ceil(C r / epsilon^2)) can be chosen independently of the orthonormal frame.
